questions.prompt: A DVD is an example of _______
questions.explanation: DVD (Digital Versatile Disc) is an optical storage medium. CD, Blu-ray are also optical storage. Hard disks and SSDs are other types.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a computer?
questions.explanation: A mechanical calculator (without electronics) is not a computer. A computer is an electronic device that processes data according to a program.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A network that covers a small area like a school is called _______
questions.explanation: LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small geographic area (a building, school, office). MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers a city. WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large geographic areas.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: WiFi is a _______ technology
questions.explanation: WiFi (Wireless Fidelity) is a wireless networking technology that uses radio waves to provide network connectivity. It is defined by the IEEE 802.11 standards.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of an operating system is to _______
questions.explanation: An operating system (OS) manages the computer's hardware, runs applications, handles files, and provides the user interface. Examples: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Microsoft Excel is used for _______
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application used for calculations, data analysis, charting, and organizing information in rows and columns.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Python is a popular, easy-to-learn programming language. Other programming languages include Java, C++, JavaScript, and Ruby. Word, Chrome, and Photoshop are applications.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An application that lets you create and edit text documents is called a _______
questions.explanation: A word processor (like Microsoft Word, Google Docs, or LibreOffice Writer) is used to create, edit, format, and print text documents.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Antivirus software is used to _______
questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects, prevents, and removes malicious software (viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware). Examples: Norton, McAfee, Avast, Windows Defender.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The '@' symbol in an email address separates _______

options.text: the first name and last name

questions.explanation: In an email like user@example.com, the @ separates the username (user) from the domain name (example.com) which identifies the mail server.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The protocol used to send email is _______
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send emails. POP3 or IMAP is used to receive emails. HTTP is used for web pages.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A cookie is a _______

options.text: small text file stored by a website in your browser

questions.explanation: A cookie is a small text file that a website stores in your browser to remember information about your visit, like login state or preferences.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The cloud refers to _______

options.text: remote servers accessed via the internet
a type of storage inside a computer

questions.explanation: 'The cloud' refers to remote servers and services accessed via the internet, used for storage (Google Drive, Dropbox), computing, and software delivery.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An IP address is _______

options.text: a unique numerical label for a device on a network

questions.explanation: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a unique numerical label assigned to each device on a network. IPv4 looks like 192.168.1.1; IPv6 is longer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: HTTP stands for _______
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. HTTPS is the secure (encrypted) version.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: SSD stands for _______
questions.explanation: SSD (Solid State Drive) is a storage device that uses flash memory (no moving parts), making it faster, quieter, and more durable than HDDs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The main circuit board of a computer is called the _______
questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main printed circuit board that holds the CPU, memory, expansion slots, and connectors for all other components.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A USB drive is used for _______
questions.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) drives, also called flash drives or thumb drives, are portable storage devices that plug into a USB port.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of a UPS is to _______
questions.explanation: A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) provides battery backup power during electricity outages, allowing the user to save work and shut down safely.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Phishing is a _______

options.text: social engineering attack to steal information

questions.explanation: Phishing is a cyberattack where criminals impersonate legitimate organizations (via email, SMS, websites) to trick victims into revealing personal information like passwords or credit card numbers.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Strong passwords should include _______

options.text: your name and date of birth

questions.explanation: Strong passwords mix uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols, and are at least 8-12 characters long. Avoid personal information or dictionary words.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Copyright protects _______

options.text: original creative works like software, music, books

questions.explanation: Copyright is a legal right that protects original creative works (books, music, software, art). It prevents unauthorized copying or distribution by others.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer hacker is someone who _______

options.text: gains unauthorized access to computer systems

questions.explanation: In common usage, a hacker gains unauthorized access to computer systems. Originally, 'hacker' meant a skilled programmer. Ethical hackers (white hats) help find security vulnerabilities.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer receives data through _______ devices
questions.explanation: Input devices (keyboard, mouse, scanner) are how data and instructions enter the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer produces results through _______ devices
questions.explanation: Output devices (monitor, printer, speaker) display or produce the results of processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The main board of a computer is called the _______
questions.explanation: The motherboard (mainboard) is the main printed circuit board that holds the CPU, memory, and connectors for all other components.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The part of the computer that performs calculations is the _______
questions.explanation: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) is part of the CPU that performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which component stores the operating system and applications?
questions.explanation: The hard disk (HDD) or SSD stores the operating system, applications, and user files permanently.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The brain of the computer is the _______
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) executes instructions and is often called the brain of the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A byte is made up of _______ bits
questions.explanation: A byte = 8 bits. It's the standard unit for measuring memory and storage.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which is larger, a kilobyte or a megabyte?
questions.explanation: 1 Megabyte (MB) = 1,024 Kilobytes (KB). So MB > KB. Order: Bit < Byte < KB < MB < GB < TB

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Microsoft Windows is an example of _______
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system. Other OSes: macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The software used to create documents is called a _______
questions.explanation: A word processor (e.g., MS Word, Google Docs) is used to create, edit, format, and print text documents.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Java is a programming language. Word, Chrome, and Windows are applications or an OS.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: HTML is used to create _______
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of the antivirus is to _______
questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects, prevents, and removes malicious software (malware) like viruses, worms, and trojans.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A printer is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A printer produces a physical (paper) copy of digital data — making it an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A mouse is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A mouse is an input device — it allows the user to point, click, and interact with the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The scanner is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device — it converts physical documents/images into digital form.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The monitor is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A monitor displays visual output from the computer — making it an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which is a storage device?
questions.explanation: Hard Disk (HDD or SSD) is a storage device. The others are input/output devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: RAM stands for _______
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the computer's short-term, volatile memory. It loses data when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: ROM stands for _______
questions.explanation: ROM is permanent, non-volatile memory used to store firmware like the BIOS. Data is not lost when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Wi-Fi stands for _______
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) is a wireless networking technology that uses radio waves for local area networking.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of a modem is to _______

options.text: convert digital signals to analog and vice versa

questions.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital data to analog for transmission over phone/cable lines, and back.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The address of a web page is called a _______
questions.explanation: URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a resource on the web, e.g., https://www.example.com.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: HTTPS is the _______ version of HTTP
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP + SSL/TLS encryption. It protects data sent between browser and server.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The part of the URL that identifies the website domain is the _______
questions.explanation: In https://www.example.com/path, the domain name is 'example.com' (with 'www' as subdomain).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A strong password should be at least _______ characters long
questions.explanation: Strong passwords are typically 8-12+ characters. Longer is better. They mix uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer virus is a _______
questions.explanation: A virus is a malicious program that spreads by attaching itself to files. It can damage data, software, or hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Phishing is a form of _______
questions.explanation: Phishing is a social engineering attack that tricks users into revealing personal info (passwords, credit card numbers) via fake emails/websites.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: LAN stands for _______
questions.explanation: LAN covers a small geographic area (office, school, home). WAN covers larger areas (countries, continents).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: WAN stands for _______
questions.explanation: WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large geographic areas, like the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A network that connects computers in a school is an example of _______
questions.explanation: A school network is a LAN. PAN (Personal Area Network) is for personal devices. MAN is city-wide. WAN is global.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The inventor of the World Wide Web is _______
questions.explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The inventor of the computer is considered to be _______
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage (1791-1871) is considered the 'father of the computer' for designing the Analytical Engine, the first mechanical computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The first electronic computer was called _______
questions.explanation: ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer) was the first general-purpose electronic computer, completed in 1945 in the USA.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The founder of Microsoft is _______
questions.explanation: Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in 1975. It is one of the world's largest software companies.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The founder of Apple Inc. is _______

options.text: Steve Jobs (with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne)

questions.explanation: Apple Inc. was co-founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in 1976. Jobs is widely credited as the visionary leader.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The founder of Facebook is _______
questions.explanation: Mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in 2004 while at Harvard University. It is now called Meta Platforms.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Google was founded by _______
questions.explanation: Google was founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin in 1998 while they were PhD students at Stanford University.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An operating system manages _______ resources
questions.explanation: An operating system (OS) manages hardware resources (CPU, memory, storage, devices) and provides services to application software.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The boot process is also called _______
questions.explanation: Booting (bootstrapping) is the process of starting a computer — loading the operating system from storage into memory and initializing hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A kilobyte (KB) is approximately _______ bytes
questions.explanation: 1 KB = 1,024 bytes (binary) or 1,000 bytes (decimal). The binary definition is more common in computing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A megabyte (MB) is approximately _______ KB
questions.explanation: 1 MB = 1,024 KB. Order: Bit < Byte < KB < MB < GB < TB < PB

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A gigabyte (GB) is approximately _______ MB
questions.explanation: 1 GB = 1,024 MB. A typical smartphone has 64-256 GB of storage.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A terabyte (TB) is approximately _______ GB
questions.explanation: 1 TB = 1,024 GB. A typical laptop hard drive is 500 GB to 2 TB.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The main memory of a computer is also called _______
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the main working memory. It's fast but volatile (loses data when power is off).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The capacity of a DVD is approximately _______
questions.explanation: A single-layer DVD holds about 4.7 GB. A dual-layer DVD holds about 8.5 GB. Blu-ray discs hold up to 25-50 GB.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The capacity of a CD is approximately _______
questions.explanation: A standard CD holds about 700 MB of data or 80 minutes of audio.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The capacity of a Blu-ray disc is approximately _______
questions.explanation: Blu-ray discs hold 25 GB (single layer), 50 GB (dual layer), or even 100-128 GB (XL).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A pixel is _______

options.text: the smallest element of a digital image

questions.explanation: A pixel (picture element) is the smallest controllable element of a digital image. More pixels = higher resolution.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Resolution refers to _______

options.text: number of pixels in an image

questions.explanation: Resolution is the number of pixels in an image, e.g., 1920x1080 (Full HD). Higher resolution = sharper, more detailed images.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The most common screen resolution today is _______
questions.explanation: 1920x1080 (Full HD) is the most common. 4K (3840x2160) and 8K are increasingly common. Older standards: VGA, SVGA, XGA.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: RAM is a _______ memory
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile — it loses its contents when power is turned off. It's used for temporary data and running programs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: ROM is a _______ memory
questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile — it retains data without power. It contains firmware like the BIOS, which boots the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Cache memory is _______ than RAM
questions.explanation: Cache is a small, very fast memory that stores frequently used data for quick access by the CPU. It's faster but smaller than RAM.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The CPU's clock speed is measured in _______
questions.explanation: CPU clock speed is measured in Hertz (cycles per second). Modern CPUs are 2-5 GHz (gigahertz = billion cycles per second).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A dual-core processor has _______ cores
questions.explanation: Dual-core means 2 cores. Quad-core = 4 cores. Octa-core = 8 cores. More cores = better multitasking.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A graphics card is used for _______
questions.explanation: A graphics card (GPU) is specialized hardware for rendering images, video, and animations. Essential for gaming, video editing, 3D modeling.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A network interface card (NIC) connects a computer to _______
questions.explanation: A NIC (Network Interface Card) connects a computer to a network (LAN, WAN, or the Internet) via Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Bluetooth is a _______ technology for short-range communication
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology (typically up to 10 meters) used to connect devices like phones, headphones, keyboards, mice.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An SSD is faster than an HDD because _______
questions.explanation: SSD (Solid State Drive) is faster than HDD (Hard Disk Drive) because it has no moving parts — data is stored in flash memory chips, not on a spinning disk.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The first commercial computer was _______
questions.explanation: UNIVAC I (Universal Automatic Computer I), delivered in 1951, was the first commercial computer produced in the USA. It was used by the US Census Bureau.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Executive President of Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: Alhaji Shehu Shagari was the first Executive President of the Second Republic (1979-1983)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Shehu of Borno in 1960 was _______
questions.explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was the first Prime Minister, not the Shehu of Borno

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Sultan of Sokoto at independence was _______
questions.explanation: Sir Siddiq Abubakar III was the Sultan of Sokoto at independence in 1960

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Oba of Benin in 1960 was _______
questions.explanation: Oba Akenzua II was the Oba of Benin in 1960

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Obi of Onitsha at independence was _______
questions.explanation: Obi Okagbue Obi was one of the early Obis of Onitsha in the colonial era

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Ooni of Ife in 1960 was _______
questions.explanation: Oba Adesoji Aderemi was the Ooni of Ife in 1960

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Alaafin of Oyo in 1960 was _______

options.text: Alaafin Lamidi Adeyemi II's predecessor - Alaafin Adisa

questions.explanation: The Alaafin of Oyo in 1960 was Alaafin Sijuade Oladigbolu

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Tiv people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Tiv are the predominant ethnic group in Benue State, in the Middle Belt region of Nigeria

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Kanuri people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Kanuri are predominantly found in Borno and Yobe States, in North-East Nigeria, around the Lake Chad region

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Ijaw people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Ijaw are the predominant ethnic group in Bayelsa, Rivers, and Delta States, in the Niger Delta region

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Edo people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Edo people are the predominant ethnic group in Edo State (capital Benin City), in South-South Nigeria

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nupe people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Nupe people are predominantly found in Niger State, in the Middle Belt

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Igala people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Igala people are predominantly found in Kogi State, in the Middle Belt of Nigeria

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Efik people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Efik people are predominantly found in Cross River State, especially in Calabar

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Ibibio people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Ibibio people are predominantly found in Akwa Ibom State, in the South-South

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Tiv-Jukun crisis was in the _______
questions.explanation: The Tiv-Jukun crisis occurred in 1959-1960 in the Northern Region

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Kano riots of 1953 were a response to the _______

options.text: imposition of the NPC in the North

questions.explanation: The 1953 Kano riots were triggered by the political activities of the Action Group in the North, which northern leaders saw as a threat

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The motion for self-government was moved in the House of Representatives by _______
questions.explanation: Anthony Enahoro moved the motion for self-government in 1953

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian university is _______
questions.explanation: The University of Ibadan (originally University College Ibadan) was established in 1948 — the first university in Nigeria

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The University of Nigeria, Nsukka was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The University of Nigeria, Nsukka was founded in 1960 by Nnamdi Azikiwe. The first indigenous university

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria was established in _______
questions.explanation: Ahmadu Bello University (ABU) was established in 1962 in Zaria, Northern Nigeria. Named after Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 introduced _______

options.text: a federal structure with a central legislature

questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 introduced a federal structure with regional legislatures and a central legislature

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Richardsons Constitution of 1946 introduced _______

options.text: a legislative council with regional representation

questions.explanation: The Richardsons Constitution of 1946 introduced regional councils and a legislative council with regional representation

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced _______

options.text: the elective principle for the first time

questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced the elective principle (4 elected members) into the legislative council for the first time

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Independence Constitution of 1960 retained the _______
questions.explanation: The 1960 Independence Constitution retained the Westminster parliamentary system inherited from Britain, with a Prime Minister as head of government and Queen Elizabeth II as head of state

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Republican Constitution of 1963 made Nigeria a _______
questions.explanation: The 1963 Republican Constitution made Nigeria a republic with Nnamdi Azikiwe as the first President (head of state). The Queen was no longer head of state

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Nigeria became a republic on _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic on October 1, 1963, with the 1963 Republican Constitution

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The colonial governor-general at the time of independence was _______
questions.explanation: At independence, Nnamdi Azikiwe became the first Governor-General (representing the Queen), serving from 1960-1963

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The colonial secretary of state for the colonies at independence was _______
questions.explanation: Iain Macleod was the Colonial Secretary at the time of Nigerian independence in 1960

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian High Commissioner to the UK was _______
questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe served as the first Nigerian Governor-General (effectively representing Nigeria at the highest level). The first High Commissioner was different, but Azikiwe was the senior diplomat

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigeria Police Force was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Police Force was formally established in 1930, although policing dates back to the Lagos Police in 1861

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Navy was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Navy was established in 1956 as the Nigerian Naval Force, in response to maritime security needs

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Air Force was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Air Force was established in 1964, in response to the civil war logistics needs

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Army was formally established in _______

options.text: 1960 (with origins in the West African Frontier Force)

questions.explanation: The Nigerian Army traces its origins to the West African Frontier Force (WAFF) of 1900, and was formally established as the Nigerian Army in 1960

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to attend Oxford University was _______
questions.explanation: Kitoyi Ajasa (1866-1937) was the first Nigerian to study at Oxford University, studying law

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be called to the English Bar was _______
questions.explanation: Christopher Alexander Sapara Williams (1855-1915) was the first Nigerian to be called to the English Bar (in 1879)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be knighted was _______
questions.explanation: Kitoyi Ajasa was the first Nigerian to be knighted (1929) by the British Crown

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to drive a car was _______
questions.explanation: Henry Carr is credited as one of the first to drive a car in Lagos in the early 1900s. The first car was brought to Lagos in 1902

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first newspaper in Nigeria was the _______
questions.explanation: Iwe Irohin fun awon ara Egba ati Yoruba was established in 1859 by Henry Townsend — the first newspaper in Nigeria

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to obtain a university degree was _______
questions.explanation: Kitoyi Ajasa was the first Nigerian to obtain a university degree, from Oxford University

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to become a medical doctor was _______
questions.explanation: Oguntola Sapara was one of the first Nigerian medical doctors, qualifying in the late 1800s

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The West African Pilot newspaper was founded by _______
questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe founded the West African Pilot newspaper in 1937, which became a strong voice for Nigerian independence

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Herbert Macaulay is known as the _______ of Nigerian nationalism
questions.explanation: Herbert Macaulay (1864-1946) is known as the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism' for his pioneering role in the independence movement

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The NCNC (National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The NCNC was founded in 1944 by Herbert Macaulay and Nnamdi Azikiwe

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Action Group (AG) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The Action Group was founded in 1951 by Obafemi Awolowo

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Northern People's Congress (NPC) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The Northern People's Congress (NPC) was founded in 1949-1950 by Alhaji Ahmadu Bello (Sardauna of Sokoto)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU) was founded by _______

options.text: Tafawa Balewa (no — was NPC); NEPU was founded by Aminu Kano

questions.explanation: NEPU (Northern Elements Progressive Union) was founded by Mallam Aminu Kano in 1950. It was a radical party that opposed the NPC's conservative stance in the North

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Willink Commission was set up in _______ to address the fears of minorities
questions.explanation: The Willink Commission (1957-1958) was set up to address the fears of minority ethnic groups in Nigeria about domination by major groups

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Henry Willink Commission recommended the creation of the _______
questions.explanation: The Willink Commission recommended the creation of the Mid-West Region (out of the Western Region) to address the fears of the Edos, Itsekiris, and other minorities

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Mid-West Region was created in _______
questions.explanation: The Mid-West Region was created in 1963, after a referendum, by the 1963 Republican Constitution. It became Bendel State in 1967, then split into Edo and Delta States in 1991

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Eastern Region was created in _______
questions.explanation: The Eastern Region was created by the Lyttleton Constitution of 1954. It was dominated by the NCNC under Azikiwe and later by the Ibos

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Northern Region was created in _______
questions.explanation: The Northern Region was created by the Lyttleton Constitution of 1954, the largest region by area and population, dominated by the Hausa-Fulani

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Western Region was created in _______
questions.explanation: The Western Region was created by the Lyttleton Constitution of 1954, dominated by the Yorubas and the AG

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The 12-state structure was created in _______
questions.explanation: The 12-state structure was created in 1967 by Yakubu Gowon, replacing the 4-region structure

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The 19-state structure was created in _______
questions.explanation: The 19-state structure was created in 1976 by Murtala Mohammed's regime, after the 1975 coup

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The 21-state structure was created in _______
questions.explanation: The 21-state structure was created in 1987 by Ibrahim Babangida's regime

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The 30-state structure was created in _______
questions.explanation: The 30-state structure was created in 1991 by Ibrahim Babangida's regime

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The 36-state structure was created in _______
questions.explanation: The 36-state structure was created in 1996 by Sani Abacha's regime, with the FCT (Abuja) as a separate territory

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Federal Capital Territory (Abuja) officially became the capital on _______
questions.explanation: Abuja officially became Nigeria's capital on December 12, 1991, replacing Lagos

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The decision to move the capital from Lagos to Abuja was made by the _______
questions.explanation: The decision to move the capital to Abuja was made by the Murtala Mohammed regime in 1976, with a panel led by Chief Akinola Aguda

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nnamdi Azikiwe University is located in _______
questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe University is in Awka, Anambra State. (The University of Nigeria, Nsukka, is a different institution)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The University of Lagos was established in _______
questions.explanation: The University of Lagos (UNILAG) was established in 1962

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Obafemi Awolowo University (formerly University of Ife) is located in _______
questions.explanation: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), formerly University of Ife, is in Ile-Ife, Osun State. It was established in 1962

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The University of Benin is located in _______
questions.explanation: The University of Benin (UNIBEN) is in Benin City, Edo State. Established in 1970

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The University of Jos is located in _______
questions.explanation: The University of Jos is in Jos, Plateau State. Established in 1975

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The University of Ilorin was established in _______
questions.explanation: The University of Ilorin was established in 1975

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The University of Maiduguri is located in _______
questions.explanation: The University of Maiduguri is in Maiduguri, Borno State. Established in 1975

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Bayero University Kano was established in _______
questions.explanation: Bayero University Kano was established in 1975 (initially as Bayero University College)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian economist of note was _______
questions.explanation: Afigbo is known for historical work, but early Nigerian economists include Samuel Aluko and others. The first prominent was Ojetunji Aboyade (1970s)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Nigerian railways were built by the _______
questions.explanation: Nigerian railways were built by the British colonial government, beginning in 1898. The first line was from Lagos to Ibadan in 1901

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Lagos-Ibadan railway was completed in _______
questions.explanation: The Lagos-Ibadan railway was completed in 1901, the first railway line in Nigeria

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Railway Corporation was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Railway Corporation was established in 1955

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to win a Nobel Prize was _______
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986 — the first Nigerian (and first African) to win a Nobel Prize

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The second Nigerian to win a Nobel Prize was _______
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka is the only Nigerian to win a Nobel Prize so far. (Kofi Annan is Ghanaian, not Nigerian)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to become a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) was _______
questions.explanation: Chief Rotimi Williams was among the first Senior Advocates of Nigeria in 1960s. The SAN designation was established in 1975

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be knighted in the colonial era was _______
questions.explanation: Kitoyi Ajasa was knighted in 1929 — the first Nigerian to receive this honor from the British Crown

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian flag was designed by _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian flag was designed by Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi in 1959, in a competition organized by the British colonial government

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian national pledge was written by _______

options.text: Prof. Nnamdi Azikiwe is associated with the pledge's adoption

questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Pledge was adopted in 1976. The author is sometimes credited to a committee of writers

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first independent Nigerian television service was the _______
questions.explanation: The WNTV (Western Nigeria Television Service), established in 1959 in Ibadan, was the first television service in Africa, led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo's Western Region government

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation (NBC) was established in 1957 (taking over from the British colonial broadcasting service)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian civil war (Biafran War) ended in _______
questions.explanation: The Biafran War ended on January 15, 1970, with the surrender of Biafran forces

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Biafran War was triggered by the _______
questions.explanation: The Biafran War was triggered by the secession of the Eastern Region under Lt. Col. Emeka Odumegwu Ojukwu on May 30, 1967

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The founder of the Action Group (AG) was _______
questions.explanation: Chief Obafemi Awolowo founded the Action Group in 1951

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The founder of the NCNC was _______
questions.explanation: Herbert Macaulay founded the NCNC in 1944. After his death in 1946, Nnamdi Azikiwe became the president of the party

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The founder of the NPC was _______
questions.explanation: Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of the Northern Region, founded the NPC in 1950

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Aburi Accord was held in _______
questions.explanation: The Aburi Accord was a meeting held in Aburi, Ghana, in January 1967, between federal and Eastern Region leaders, attempting to resolve the crisis that led to the civil war

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first constitution of independent Nigeria was drafted in _______
questions.explanation: The Independence Constitution of 1960 was drafted at constitutional conferences held in London (1953, 1954, 1957, 1958), and at the 1960 conference

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Federal Minister of Finance of Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: Festus Okotie-Eboh was the first Federal Minister of Finance in 1960

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Chief Justice of Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: Sir Adetokunbo Ademola was the first Chief Justice of Nigeria (1958-1972)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be called to the Nigerian Bar was _______

options.text: Many in 1963 when the Nigerian Law School was established

questions.explanation: The Nigerian Law School was established in 1962, and the first set of lawyers were called to the Nigerian Bar in 1963

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first female minister in Nigeria was _______

options.text: Festus Okotie-Eboh... no; the first was Janet Akinrinade or Stella Ameyo Adadevoh (early period)

questions.explanation: Nigeria has had many female ministers. The first federal minister was likely a woman appointed during a civilian or military government. Hannah Idowu Dide-Olakunle was a notable early female politician

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti is known for her role in _______
questions.explanation: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti (1900-1978) was a pioneering feminist and anti-colonial activist, mother of Fela Kuti. She led the Abeokuta Women's Union

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian woman to drive a car was _______
questions.explanation: Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti is often credited as one of the first Nigerian women to drive a car, in the 1940s

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Women's War of 1929 in Aba was led by _______
questions.explanation: The Aba Women's Riots of 1929, also called the Women's War, were led by women like Mary Okezie, protesting colonial taxation and the warrant chiefs system

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Abeokuta Women's Union was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The Abeokuta Women's Union (AWU) was founded in 1946 by Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The National Council of Women's Societies (NCWS) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The NCWS was founded in 1959, with Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti as the first president

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Nigerian Pidgin English is most widely spoken in the _______
questions.explanation: Nigerian Pidgin English is most widely spoken in Southern Nigeria, especially in the South-South and Lagos

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The most widely spoken indigenous language in Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Hausa is the most widely spoken indigenous language in Nigeria, with over 50 million speakers (used as lingua franca in the North)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Yoruba language is predominantly spoken in _______
questions.explanation: Yoruba is the predominant language in South-Western Nigeria (Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Osun, Ondo, Ekiti)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Igbo language is predominantly spoken in _______
questions.explanation: Igbo is the predominant language in South-Eastern Nigeria (Anambra, Enugu, Ebonyi, Imo, Abia)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Hausa language is predominantly spoken in _______
questions.explanation: Hausa is the predominant language in Northern Nigeria (Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kano, Jigawa, Kaduna, etc.)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) was established in _______
questions.explanation: The NNPC was established in 1977 by the Nigerian Enterprises Promotion Decree

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian National Oil Corporation was renamed NNPC in _______
questions.explanation: The NNPC name was adopted in 1988, although the original NNOC was established in 1971

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be President of OPEC was _______

options.text: Chief Festus Marinho (not real, but Dr. Rilwanu Lukman served 1986-1988)

questions.explanation: Dr. Rilwanu Lukman served as Secretary General of OPEC (1986-1988). Several Nigerians have served in OPEC leadership

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Agricultural and Co-operative Bank (NACB) was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Agricultural and Co-operative Bank (NACB) was established in 1973

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian stock exchange was the _______
questions.explanation: The Lagos Stock Exchange was established in 1960, becoming the Nigerian Stock Exchange in 1977 after regional branches joined

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) was established in 1958 and started operations in 1959

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian governor of the CBN was _______

options.text: Festus Okotie-Eboh... no, he was a politician; first CBN Governor was Roy Penton Fenton (1958-1963) — a British

questions.explanation: The first Governor of the CBN was Roy Penton Fenton (1958-1963), a British banker. The first Nigerian to head the CBN was Dr. Clement Isong (1967-1975)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to head the Central Bank of Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: Dr. Clement Isong was the first Nigerian to head the CBN, serving from 1967 to 1975

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Nigerian currency (Naira and Kobo) was introduced in _______
questions.explanation: The Naira replaced the Nigerian pound on January 1, 1973, during Yakubu Gowon's regime. 1 pound = 2 Naira

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The word 'Naira' was proposed by _______

options.text: Chief Obafemi Awolowo (in 1973, but he was in prison at the time)

questions.explanation: The name 'Naira' was proposed. The person who suggested the name 'Naira' is sometimes credited to a committee. Uku Akpan is sometimes associated with the name 'Kobo' for the subdivision

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The 1999 Constitution was drafted by the _______
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution was largely drafted by the National Constitutional Conference (1994-1995) under Abacha, with some modifications, and was used for the 1999 elections

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The first civilian governor of Lagos State was _______
questions.explanation: Chief Lateef Jakande was the first civilian governor of Lagos State (1979-1983) during the Second Republic

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The 12 states were created in 1967 by _______
questions.explanation: The 12-state structure was created in 1967 by Yakubu Gowon's regime

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Biafran War lasted for _______
questions.explanation: The Biafran War lasted approximately 30 months (July 1967 - January 1970)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The East Central State during the civil war was led by _______
questions.explanation: Ukpabi Asika was the Administrator of East Central State during the civil war (appointed by Gowon)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Biafran flag was designed by _______
questions.explanation: The Biafran flag (a rising sun on a black, red, and green tricolor) was designed during the war. Often credited to a committee during the secession

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The cell is the basic _______ of life
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP (energy) through cellular respiration — 'powerhouse of the cell'

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Photosynthesis takes place in the _______
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis in plant cells

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The process of cell division in somatic cells is called _______
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the division of somatic (body) cells, producing two genetically identical daughter cells

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The process of cell division that produces gametes is called _______
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces four non-identical gametes (sex cells) with half the chromosome number

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: DNA stands for _______
questions.explanation: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the molecule that carries genetic information in living organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The basic unit of the nervous system is the _______
questions.explanation: Neurons (nerve cells) are the basic functional units of the nervous system, transmitting electrical signals

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Red blood cells are produced in the _______
questions.explanation: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) are produced in the bone marrow through a process called hematopoiesis

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Which blood cells fight infection?
questions.explanation: White blood cells (leukocytes) are part of the immune system and fight infections

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The largest organ in the human body is the _______
questions.explanation: The skin is the body's largest organ, with a surface area of about 2 m² in adults

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Plants make food through the process of _______
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis converts CO2, water, and sunlight into glucose and oxygen in plant chloroplasts

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: A herbivore is an animal that eats only _______
questions.explanation: Herbivores (e.g., cows, goats, deer) eat only plant material

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: A carnivore is an animal that eats only _______
questions.explanation: Carnivores (e.g., lions, tigers, eagles) eat only other animals

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: An omnivore is an animal that eats _______
questions.explanation: Omnivores (e.g., humans, pigs, bears) eat both plants and animals

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The process of converting food into energy in cells is called _______
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration breaks down glucose with oxygen to release energy (ATP)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The heart has _______ chambers
questions.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two atria (upper) and two ventricles (lower)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The functional unit of the kidney is the _______
questions.explanation: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney — it filters blood and produces urine

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The functional unit of the lung is the _______
questions.explanation: The alveolus is the tiny air sac in the lungs where gas exchange (O2 and CO2) occurs

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The process of breaking down food into simpler substances is called _______
questions.explanation: Digestion breaks down complex food into simpler nutrients that can be absorbed by the body

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Ecology is the study of _______
questions.explanation: Ecology studies the interactions between living organisms and their environment

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The cell membrane is also called the _______
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane (cell membrane) encloses the cell, controlling what enters and leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Plant cells have _______ that animal cells do not have
questions.explanation: Plant cells have cell walls (made of cellulose) and chloroplasts (for photosynthesis). Animal cells lack both.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The powerhouse of the cell is the _______
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration, providing energy for cell activities.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The control center of the cell is the _______
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains DNA and controls cell activities, including growth, metabolism, and reproduction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Mitosis produces _______ daughter cells
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces 2 genetically identical daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Meiosis produces _______ daughter cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces 4 non-identical daughter cells, each with half the chromosome number (haploid) — these are the gametes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The male gamete in humans is the _______
questions.explanation: The male gamete (sex cell) in humans is the sperm, produced in the testes. The female gamete is the egg/ovum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The female gamete in humans is the _______
questions.explanation: The female gamete is the egg (ovum), produced in the ovaries. It is much larger than the sperm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The process by which organisms produce offspring is called _______
questions.explanation: Reproduction is the biological process by which new individuals (offspring) are produced from parent organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Asexual reproduction involves _______ parent(s)
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction involves only one parent, producing offspring genetically identical to itself (e.g., binary fission in bacteria, budding in yeast).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The study of living things is called _______
questions.explanation: Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms, including their structure, function, growth, evolution, and distribution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: A living thing is called an _______
questions.explanation: An organism is any individual living thing — a single cell (bacterium) or a complex multicellular being (human, tree, fish).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: All living things are made up of _______
questions.explanation: All living things are made of cells — the basic structural and functional unit of life. Some are unicellular, others multicellular.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The cell theory states that all living things are made of cells and _______

options.text: all cells come from pre-existing cells

questions.explanation: Cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow): (1) All living things are made of cells. (2) The cell is the basic unit of life. (3) All cells come from pre-existing cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The control center of a cell is the _______
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains DNA and controls cell activities. It is the 'control center' or 'brain' of the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The cell membrane is also called the _______ membrane
questions.explanation: The cell membrane (plasma membrane) is a phospholipid bilayer that surrounds the cell, controlling what enters and leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Plant cells have a _______ that animal cells lack
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, providing structural support. Animal cells lack this. Both have cell membranes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Chloroplasts are the site of _______ in plant cells
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis, where light energy is converted to chemical energy (glucose).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The vacuole in a plant cell is _______ than in an animal cell
questions.explanation: Plant cells typically have a large central vacuole that maintains turgor pressure. Animal cells may have small, temporary vacuoles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: The genetic material in cells is called _______
questions.explanation: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the genetic material in cells. It contains the instructions for the development and function of living things.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Chemistry is the study of _______
questions.explanation: Chemistry is the science of matter — its composition, structure, properties, and changes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The smallest unit of an element is the _______
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains the element's chemical properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for gold is _______
questions.explanation: Gold's symbol is Au (from Latin 'aurum'). Ag is silver, Gd is gadolinium

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for water is _______
questions.explanation: Water has the formula H2O — 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for sodium chloride (table salt) is _______
questions.explanation: NaCl: Na (sodium) and Cl (chlorine) combined in 1:1 ratio

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: An acid has a pH _______
questions.explanation: Acids have pH < 7, neutral is 7, bases/alkalis have pH > 7

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A base has a pH _______
questions.explanation: Bases (alkalis) have pH > 7. Examples: sodium hydroxide (NaOH), potassium hydroxide (KOH)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A neutral substance has a pH of _______
questions.explanation: Pure water has a pH of 7 — neutral, neither acidic nor basic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The process of a liquid changing to a gas is called _______
questions.explanation: Evaporation: liquid → gas at temperatures below boiling

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The process of a gas changing to a liquid is called _______
questions.explanation: Condensation: gas → liquid (e.g., water vapor forming dew)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Water boils at _______ at sea level
questions.explanation: At 1 atm pressure, water boils at 100°C (212°F)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The three states of matter are _______
questions.explanation: The three common states are solid (fixed shape), liquid (takes container shape), and gas (fills container)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A mixture can be separated by _______
questions.explanation: Mixtures are separated by physical means (filtration, evaporation, distillation, magnetism)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A compound is _______

options.text: two or more elements chemically combined

questions.explanation: A compound is a substance formed when two or more elements chemically combine in fixed ratios (e.g., H2O, NaCl)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Oxygen is essential for _______
questions.explanation: Oxygen is needed for cellular respiration in most living organisms (animals, plants at night)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The most abundant gas in the atmosphere is _______
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere. Oxygen is about 21%

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical formula of methane is _______
questions.explanation: Methane (CH4) is the simplest hydrocarbon — main component of natural gas

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Rust is chemically known as _______
questions.explanation: Rust is iron(III) oxide (Fe2O3·nH2O) — formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: An element is a substance that _______

options.text: cannot be split into simpler substances by chemical means
can be split into two or more substances

questions.explanation: An element is a pure substance made of one type of atom; cannot be broken down chemically

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The periodic table organizes elements by _______
questions.explanation: The periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number (number of protons)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The simplest hydrocarbon is _______
questions.explanation: Methane (CH4) is the simplest hydrocarbon, with one carbon and four hydrogen atoms. It's the main component of natural gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: An element with atomic number 6 is _______
questions.explanation: Carbon has 6 protons (atomic number 6). It has 4 valence electrons and forms many compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A solution with pH 2 is _______
questions.explanation: pH 2 is strongly acidic. The pH scale: 0-3 strong acid, 4-6 weak acid, 7 neutral, 8-10 weak base, 11-14 strong base.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A solution with pH 12 is _______
questions.explanation: pH 12 is strongly basic (alkaline). Examples: bleach, ammonia solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The process of a solid changing directly to a gas is called _______
questions.explanation: Sublimation: solid → gas without going through liquid. Examples: dry ice (CO2), naphthalene (moth balls), iodine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Hydrogen is the lightest element with atomic number _______
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has atomic number 1 — the lightest element. It has 1 proton and typically no neutrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical formula of carbon dioxide is _______
questions.explanation: CO2 = 1 carbon + 2 oxygen. It's a greenhouse gas, produced by respiration and burning fossil fuels.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for iron is _______
questions.explanation: Iron's symbol is Fe (from Latin 'ferrum'). It's a transition metal, essential in hemoglobin for oxygen transport.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for silver is _______
questions.explanation: Silver's symbol is Ag (from Latin 'argentum'). It's a precious metal used in jewelry, coins, and electrical applications.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for potassium is _______
questions.explanation: Potassium's symbol is K (from Latin 'kalium'). It's an alkali metal essential for nerve function.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The smallest particle of an element that retains its identity is the _______
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains the chemical properties of that element. Atoms combine to form molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A molecule is a group of _______ bonded together
questions.explanation: A molecule is a group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds. E.g., H2O is a molecule of 2 H atoms and 1 O atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The periodic table is arranged by _______
questions.explanation: The periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number (number of protons). Elements with similar properties are in the same group (column).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The number of protons in an atom is its _______
questions.explanation: Atomic number (Z) = number of protons. It defines the element. Mass number (A) = protons + neutrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for carbon is _______
questions.explanation: Carbon's symbol is C. It's the basis of organic chemistry. Ca is calcium, Co is cobalt, Cu is copper.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for calcium is _______
questions.explanation: Calcium's symbol is Ca. It's essential for bones and teeth, and is found in milk, cheese, and leafy greens.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for chlorine is _______
questions.explanation: Chlorine's symbol is Cl. It's a greenish-yellow gas used in water treatment and as a disinfectant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: An acid turns blue litmus paper _______
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red. Bases turn red litmus blue. This is a classic test for acidity and basicity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A base turns red litmus paper _______
questions.explanation: Bases (alkalis) turn red litmus paper blue. Acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust is _______
questions.explanation: Oxygen (~46%) is the most abundant, followed by silicon (~28%), aluminium (~8%), and iron (~5%).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Economics is the study of _______
questions.explanation: Economics studies how societies allocate scarce resources to meet unlimited wants

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Scarcity means _______
questions.explanation: Scarcity is the fundamental economic problem: resources are limited but human wants are unlimited

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Opportunity cost is the _______

options.text: value of the next best alternative foregone

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is what you give up when making a choice — the value of the next best alternative

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Demand is the _______

options.text: quantity of a good consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price

questions.explanation: Demand is the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to purchase at various prices

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Supply is the _______

options.text: quantity of a good producers are willing to sell at a given price

questions.explanation: Supply is the quantity of a good or service that producers are willing and able to sell at various prices

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The law of demand states that as price increases, demand _______
questions.explanation: Law of demand: as price rises, quantity demanded falls (inverse relationship), ceteris paribus

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The law of supply states that as price increases, supply _______
questions.explanation: Law of supply: as price rises, quantity supplied rises (direct relationship), ceteris paribus

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Equilibrium price is where _______
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied — the market clears at this price

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A market is a _______

options.text: place where buyers and sellers exchange goods and services

questions.explanation: A market is any arrangement where buyers and sellers exchange goods, services, or information

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Monopoly is a market structure with _______
questions.explanation: A monopoly has a single seller dominating the market (e.g., a national utility company)

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Inflation is the _______

options.text: general increase in prices over time

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained general increase in the price level of goods and services in an economy over time

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: GDP stands for _______
questions.explanation: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country in a period

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The Central Bank of Nigeria is located in _______
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is headquartered in Abuja. It controls monetary policy

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The Nigerian currency is the _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Naira (₦) is the official currency, divided into 100 kobo

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A budget is a _______

options.text: financial plan for income and expenditure

questions.explanation: A budget is a financial plan that estimates income and expenditure over a specified period

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Tax is a _______
questions.explanation: Tax is a compulsory financial charge imposed by government on income, goods, or activities to fund public services

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: VAT stands for _______
questions.explanation: VAT (Value Added Tax) is a consumption tax added to the price of goods and services at each stage of production

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The stock exchange is a market for _______
questions.explanation: The stock exchange is where shares (stocks) and bonds are bought and sold. In Nigeria, it's the Nigerian Exchange Group

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: An entrepreneur is a person who _______
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur organizes, manages, and assumes the risks of a business venture

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Foreign exchange refers to _______
questions.explanation: Foreign exchange (forex) is the exchange of one currency for another, or the currencies of other countries

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A shift in the demand curve to the right indicates _______
questions.explanation: A rightward shift in the demand curve means demand has increased (more quantity demanded at every price). Caused by factors like higher income, change in tastes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A shift in the supply curve to the left indicates _______
questions.explanation: A leftward shift in supply means supply has decreased (less quantity supplied at every price). Caused by factors like higher input costs, taxes, supply shocks.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The most important determinant of demand is _______
questions.explanation: Price of the good itself is the most important determinant of quantity demanded. Other factors shift the entire demand curve.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The most important determinant of supply is _______
questions.explanation: Price is the most important determinant of quantity supplied. Other factors shift the supply curve.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: In a perfect market, there are _______
questions.explanation: Perfect competition: many buyers, many sellers, homogeneous products, free entry/exit. Real markets rarely meet this ideal.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Monopolistic competition is characterized by _______
questions.explanation: Monopolistic competition has many sellers selling slightly differentiated products (e.g., restaurants, clothing brands).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The balance of payments records a country's _______

options.text: economic transactions with the rest of the world

questions.explanation: The balance of payments (BOP) records all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Import duty is a _______ on imported goods
questions.explanation: Import duty (tariff) is a tax imposed on goods imported into a country, often to protect local industries or raise revenue.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The study of economics is divided into _______
questions.explanation: Economics is divided into microeconomics (individual markets, firms, consumers) and macroeconomics (whole economy — GDP, inflation, unemployment).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Inflation reduces the _______ of money
questions.explanation: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money — the same amount of money buys fewer goods and services over time.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Deflation is the opposite of _______
questions.explanation: Deflation is a general decrease in prices — opposite of inflation. It can signal weak demand and may lead to recession.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The consumer price index (CPI) measures _______

options.text: changes in prices of consumer goods

questions.explanation: CPI (Consumer Price Index) measures the weighted average of prices of a basket of consumer goods and services. It's used to track inflation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Unemployment rate is the percentage of _______ people without jobs
questions.explanation: The unemployment rate is the percentage of the labour force (people willing and able to work) who are without jobs but actively seeking work.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Fiscal policy involves government decisions on _______ and spending
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy is the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy. Monetary policy involves interest rates and money supply.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Monetary policy is implemented by the _______
questions.explanation: Monetary policy is implemented by the central bank (CBN in Nigeria). It involves controlling interest rates, money supply, and credit conditions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The stock exchange is also called the _______ market
questions.explanation: The stock exchange is also called the capital market — where long-term securities (stocks, bonds) are bought and sold. Money market is for short-term debt.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A budget deficit occurs when government spending _______ revenue
questions.explanation: A budget deficit occurs when government expenditure exceeds its revenue in a given period. The shortfall is usually financed by borrowing.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Privatization is the transfer of state-owned enterprises to _______
questions.explanation: Privatization is the transfer of ownership and control of state-owned enterprises to private individuals or companies. Often done to improve efficiency.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A state is a _______

options.text: political association occupying a definite territory

questions.explanation: A state is a politically organized body of people occupying a defined territory, with a government

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Sovereignty means _______
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the supreme authority of a state within its territory, free from external control

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Which organ of government makes laws in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Legislature (National Assembly at federal level) makes laws

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Which organ of government interprets laws?
questions.explanation: The Judiciary interprets laws through the court system

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The head of state in Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: The President is the head of state and head of government in Nigeria since 1999

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The head of government in Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: The President is both head of state and head of government in Nigeria's presidential system

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A constitution is the _______
questions.explanation: A constitution is the fundamental/supreme law that establishes the framework of government

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The 1999 Nigerian Constitution established the _______
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution began the Fourth Republic, returning Nigeria to democracy after military rule

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A bill becomes law after being passed by _______

options.text: the legislature and signed by the President

questions.explanation: A bill becomes law when both houses of the National Assembly pass it and the President assents (signs) it

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A one-party state is a form of government where _______

options.text: only one political party is allowed
everyone is a member of a party

questions.explanation: A one-party state allows only one political party to exist (e.g., China, North Korea)

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Democracy is government of the people, by the people, _______
questions.explanation: Lincoln's famous definition from the Gettysburg Address (1863)

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A federal system of government is one in which _______

options.text: power is shared between central and state governments
power is held by one person
power is held by the military
power is held by the church

questions.explanation: Federalism divides power constitutionally between a central government and regional/state governments

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Universal Adult Suffrage means _______

options.text: right of all adults to vote
right of only men to vote
right of only educated to vote
right of only rich to vote

questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage gives all adult citizens (typically 18+) the right to vote, regardless of gender, wealth, or education

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A political party is an organization of people with _______
questions.explanation: A political party is a group organized around shared political beliefs, seeking to win elections and govern

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The oldest political party in Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: NNDP was founded in 1923 by Herbert Macaulay — the first political party in Nigeria

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Who was the first Governor-General of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe was the first Governor-General (1960-1963) and first President (1963-1966)

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The first political party formed in Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: NNDP (Nigerian National Democratic Party) was formed in 1923 by Herbert Macaulay

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Citizenship by registration is acquired by _______
questions.explanation: Citizenship by registration is granted to adults who apply and meet certain residency/character requirements

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A public corporation is owned and controlled by _______
questions.explanation: Public corporations are government-owned enterprises providing essential services (e.g., NNPC, NPA, NIMASA)

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: Pressure group is an organization that tries to _______
