questions.explanation: Pressure groups (e.g., NLC, ASUU, NBA) influence government decisions but do not seek to form the government themselves

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The civil service is the body of _______
questions.explanation: The civil service consists of permanent, non-political government employees who implement policies

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: An election is a process of _______
questions.explanation: An election is a formal process where citizens choose their leaders or decide on issues by voting

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A voter is a person who is _______

options.text: eligible to vote in an election

questions.explanation: A voter is a person who has the legal right to cast a vote in an election

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A constituency is a _______
questions.explanation: A constituency is a geographic area from which a representative is elected

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The party with the majority in the legislature forms the _______
questions.explanation: The majority party in the legislature typically forms the government; others form the opposition

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The arms of government are _______ in number
questions.explanation: The three arms are Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary. Each has separate powers to prevent abuse.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A bicameral legislature has _______ chambers
questions.explanation: Bicameral = two chambers. Nigeria's National Assembly has Senate and House of Representatives. USA, UK, India are bicameral.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A unicameral legislature has _______ chamber(s)
questions.explanation: Unicameral = one chamber. Countries like New Zealand, Sweden, and some others have unicameral legislatures.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A bill that has been passed by the legislature and signed by the President becomes a(n) _______
questions.explanation: A bill passed by both chambers and signed by the President becomes an Act of Parliament (law).

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The minimum age to be elected President of Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: By Section 131 of the 1999 Constitution, a presidential candidate must be at least 35 years old.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A person contesting for the office of Governor in a Nigerian state must be at least _______ years old
questions.explanation: Same as the President — minimum 35 years for Governor (Section 177 of the 1999 Constitution).

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A public corporation is established by _______

options.text: an Act of Parliament or decree

questions.explanation: Public corporations are established by Acts of Parliament (or decrees, in military eras) and owned by government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The Civil Service is a _______ institution
questions.explanation: The civil service is a permanent, non-political, professional institution that implements government policies regardless of which party is in power.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A republic is a state where _______

options.text: power is held by the people and their elected representatives

questions.explanation: A republic is a state where power rests with the body of citizens entitled to vote, and is exercised by elected representatives. The head of state is usually a president, not a monarch.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A confederation is a union of _______

options.text: states with a weak central government

questions.explanation: A confederation is a loose union of sovereign states with a weak central authority. States retain most powers. Examples: EU (partially), early USA under Articles of Confederation.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A unitary state has _______

options.text: a strong central government with regional subdivisions

questions.explanation: A unitary state has a strong central government that may create regional subdivisions (states, provinces) but these have only the powers the central government grants them. Examples: France, Japan.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A federation is a state with _______

options.text: power divided between central and regional governments

questions.explanation: A federation divides power constitutionally between a central (federal) government and regional (state) governments. Both have sovereignty in their areas. Examples: USA, Nigeria, India, Brazil.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The head of state in a parliamentary system is usually a _______
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the head of state (e.g., president or monarch) is mostly ceremonial, while the Prime Minister holds executive power as head of government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The head of government in a parliamentary system is the _______
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the Prime Minister is the head of government. They lead the executive branch and are usually the leader of the majority party in parliament.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The civil service is part of the _______ arm of government
questions.explanation: The civil service is part of the executive arm. They are permanent, non-political employees who implement government policies and run the day-to-day affairs of government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: A bill of rights is a statement of _______

options.text: fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens

questions.explanation: A bill of rights is a formal declaration of the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens, usually enshrined in the constitution.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The first political party in Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) was founded in 1923 by Herbert Macaulay — the first political party in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Government
questions.prompt: The Action Group (AG) was founded in 1951 by _______
questions.explanation: The Action Group (AG) was founded in 1951 by Chief Obafemi Awolowo. It was the leading party in the Western Region.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The SI unit of length is the _______
questions.explanation: The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The SI unit of mass is the _______
questions.explanation: The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of mass

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The SI unit of time is the _______
questions.explanation: The second (s) is the SI base unit of time

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Force is measured in _______
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). 1 N = 1 kg·m/s²

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Energy is measured in _______
questions.explanation: Energy (and work) is measured in joules (J). 1 J = 1 N·m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Power is measured in _______
questions.explanation: Power is measured in watts (W). 1 W = 1 J/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The speed of light is approximately _______
questions.explanation: Light travels at approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s (300,000 km/s) in vacuum

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Acceleration is the rate of change of _______
questions.explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity / time. Measured in m/s²

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of _______
questions.explanation: Newton's first law: an object at rest stays at rest, an object in motion stays in motion, unless acted on by a net force (inertia)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Newton's second law of motion is F = _______
questions.explanation: F = m × a (Force equals mass times acceleration)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Newton's third law of motion states that for every action, there is an _______
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately _______
questions.explanation: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (or 10 m/s² for simple calculations) near Earth's surface

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Work is done when _______

options.text: a force moves an object through a distance
a force is applied but no motion

questions.explanation: Work = Force × Distance (in the direction of force). W = Fd

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Sound cannot travel through a _______
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a medium. Light can travel through vacuum; sound cannot

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Light travels in _______ lines
questions.explanation: In a uniform medium, light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The angle of incidence equals the angle of _______
questions.explanation: Law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection (measured from the normal)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The splitting of white light into seven colors is called _______
questions.explanation: Dispersion separates white light into its component colors (ROYGBIV) — like a prism or rainbow

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of electric current is the _______
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes (A). 1 A = 1 C/s (coulomb per second)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of electric potential difference is the _______
questions.explanation: Voltage (potential difference) is measured in volts (V). 1 V = 1 J/C

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of electrical resistance is the _______
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω). 1 Ω = 1 V/A (Ohm's law: V = IR)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Distance is a _______ quantity
questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar quantity — it has only magnitude, not direction. Displacement is a vector.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Displacement is a _______ quantity
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector — it has magnitude and direction. It's the straight-line distance from start to end.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Velocity is the rate of change of _______
questions.explanation: Velocity = change in displacement / time. It's a vector. Speed = distance / time (scalar).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Speed is a _______ quantity
questions.explanation: Speed is scalar (magnitude only). Velocity is vector (magnitude + direction).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The slope of a distance-time graph gives _______
questions.explanation: The slope of a distance-time (or displacement-time) graph equals the speed (or velocity).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives _______
questions.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph equals acceleration. The area under the graph gives distance/displacement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of pressure is the _______
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa). 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Other units: bar, atmosphere (atm), mmHg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Atmospheric pressure is measured using a _______
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. A manometer measures gas pressure in a container. A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of frequency is the _______
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz) = 1 cycle per second. Common multiples: kHz, MHz, GHz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Sound frequency is measured in _______
questions.explanation: Frequency of sound is in Hz. Loudness (intensity) is in decibels (dB). The human ear hears 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The SI unit of temperature is the _______
questions.explanation: The SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin (K). 0 K is absolute zero. Celsius is commonly used but not the SI base.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of electric charge is the _______
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C). 1 C = charge of ~6.24 × 10^18 electrons. The ampere is current (charge per time).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of force is the _______
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). 1 N = 1 kg·m/s². F = m × a (Newton's second law).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of energy is the _______
questions.explanation: Energy and work are measured in joules (J). 1 J = 1 N·m. Other energy units: calorie, kilowatt-hour (kWh), electron-volt (eV).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The unit of power is the _______
questions.explanation: Power is measured in watts (W). 1 W = 1 J/s. Power = energy / time. 1 kilowatt (kW) = 1000 W. 1 horsepower ≈ 746 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The first law of thermodynamics states that energy is _______
questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another. Total energy is constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The second law of thermodynamics states that entropy _______
questions.explanation: The second law: in any energy transfer, some energy becomes unusable, and entropy (disorder) of an isolated system tends to increase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The absolute zero of temperature is _______
questions.explanation: Absolute zero is 0 K = -273.15°C, the lowest possible temperature where molecular motion stops (theoretically).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Sound is a _______ wave
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a medium (solid, liquid, gas) to travel. It cannot travel through vacuum. Light is electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The speed of sound in air at room temperature is approximately _______
questions.explanation: The speed of sound in air at 20°C is about 343 m/s (1235 km/h). It's faster in solids and liquids, slower in gases.

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The process by which plants make their own food is called _______
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process where green plants use sunlight, water, and CO2 to make glucose and oxygen

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants release oxygen (O2) as a byproduct of photosynthesis. They use CO2

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The SI unit of length is the _______
questions.explanation: The metre (m) is the SI unit of length. The kilogram is for mass, second for time

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The SI unit of mass is the _______
questions.explanation: The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of mass. 1 kg = 1000 g

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is renewable — the sun is not depleted by use. Coal, petroleum, and natural gas are fossil fuels (non-renewable)

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The gas we breathe in is _______
questions.explanation: We breathe in oxygen (O2) and breathe out carbon dioxide (CO2). The air is ~78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a mammal?
questions.explanation: Mammals are warm-blooded, have hair/fur, and feed young with milk. Whales are mammals (live in water but are warm-blooded and nurse young)

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The largest organ in the human body is the _______
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ, covering the entire body and protecting internal structures

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: An adult human has 206 bones. Babies are born with about 270, but many fuse as they grow

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for water is _______
questions.explanation: Water has the chemical formula H2O: two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The chemical symbol for sodium chloride (table salt) is _______
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride is NaCl: one sodium (Na) and one chlorine (Cl) atom

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a solid?
questions.explanation: Ice is water in solid form. Water is liquid, steam and oxygen are gases

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Force is measured in _______
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). 1 N is the force needed to accelerate 1 kg at 1 m/s²

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The speed of light is approximately _______
questions.explanation: Light travels at approximately 300,000 km/s (more precisely 299,792 km/s) in vacuum

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars appears red because of iron oxide (rust) on its surface. Hence the name 'Red Planet'

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The closest star to Earth (other than the Sun) is _______
questions.explanation: Proxima Centauri is the closest known star to the Sun at about 4.24 light-years away

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Water boils at _______ at sea level
questions.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure (sea level), pure water boils at 100°C (212°F)

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Water freezes at _______ at sea level
questions.explanation: At standard pressure, pure water freezes at 0°C (32°F)

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The three states of matter are _______
questions.explanation: The three common states of matter are solid (fixed shape), liquid (takes container shape), and gas (fills container)

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: A lever is an example of a _______
questions.explanation: A lever is one of the six classical simple machines (along with inclined plane, wedge, screw, pulley, wheel and axle)

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: An example of a chemical change is _______
questions.explanation: Burning wood is a chemical change — new substances (ash, smoke, CO2) are formed and the change is irreversible. Melting ice and boiling water are physical changes

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: A mixture of salt and water can be separated by _______
questions.explanation: Evaporation separates salt from salt water — water evaporates, salt is left behind. Filtration works for insoluble solids in liquids

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The process of a liquid changing to a gas is called _______
questions.explanation: Evaporation is liquid → gas. Condensation is gas → liquid. Freezing is liquid → solid

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The process of a gas changing to a liquid is called _______
questions.explanation: Condensation is gas → liquid (e.g., water vapor on a cold glass). It's the reverse of evaporation

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a non-living thing?
questions.explanation: A rock is non-living — it doesn't grow, breathe, reproduce, or respond to stimuli like living things do

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates have a backbone. Cats are mammals (vertebrates). Snails, earthworms, and jellyfish are invertebrates

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: The main function of the heart is to _______
questions.explanation: The heart's main function is to pump blood throughout the body, delivering oxygen and nutrients

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Which part of the plant makes food?
questions.explanation: Leaves make food through photosynthesis. The flat shape and chlorophyll in leaves help capture sunlight

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Roots of plants function in _______
questions.explanation: Plant roots absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil. They also anchor the plant

questions.subject: Basic Science
questions.prompt: Energy from the sun is called _______
questions.explanation: Solar energy is energy from the sun's light and heat. It can be converted to electricity via solar panels

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A citizen is a person who legally belongs to a country by _______
questions.explanation: Citizenship is acquired by birth (to Nigerian parents), registration (as an adult), or naturalization. Birth is the most common and primary way.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a right of a citizen?

options.text: Right to refuse to pay tax

questions.explanation: Every Nigerian citizen has the right to education under the constitution. The others are not legally guaranteed rights.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The process of becoming a citizen of a country by application is called _______
questions.explanation: Naturalization is the legal process by which a foreign national acquires citizenship of a country through formal application.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: One duty of a citizen is to _______
questions.explanation: Paying taxes is a fundamental civic duty. Tax revenue funds public services like roads, schools, and hospitals.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Dual citizenship means _______

options.text: being a citizen of two countries

questions.explanation: Dual citizenship means a person is legally a citizen of two countries at the same time, holding citizenship rights in both.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The symbol on a Nigerian passport that identifies it is the _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian coat of arms appears on the official passport. It is the legal symbol of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a qualification for becoming the President of Nigeria?

options.text: Must be a citizen by birth

questions.explanation: By the Nigerian Constitution (Section 131), the President must be a citizen of Nigeria by birth, at least 35 years old, and a member of a political party.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The total number of states in Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. The last state creation was in 1996.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The supreme law of Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: The Constitution is the supreme law. Any law inconsistent with it is null and void to the extent of that inconsistency.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Rule of law means _______

options.text: everyone is equal before the law
the president is above the law

questions.explanation: Rule of law is the principle that all persons, institutions, and entities are accountable to laws that are publicly disclosed, equally enforced, and independently adjudicated.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Which arm of government makes laws in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Legislature (National Assembly: Senate + House of Representatives at federal level, State Assemblies at state level) is responsible for making laws.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Which arm of government interprets laws?
questions.explanation: The Judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes through the court system. The Supreme Court is the highest court.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The constitution was amended in 1999 to usher in _______
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution marked the start of Nigeria's Fourth Republic and the return to democratic civilian rule after years of military rule.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Fundamental Rights of citizens are contained in _______
questions.explanation: Chapter IV of the 1999 Nigerian Constitution (Sections 33-46) contains the Fundamental Rights, including right to life, dignity, personal liberty, fair hearing, etc.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A person accused of a crime is innocent until _______
questions.explanation: This is a cornerstone of the rule of law and justice system. The burden of proof lies with the prosecution.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian national anthem was composed by _______

options.text: John A. Ileogben (lyrics), F. R. Echezona (music)

questions.explanation: The current anthem 'Arise, O Compatriots' has lyrics by John A. Ileogben and music composed by F. R. Echezona, adopted in 1978.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The motto of Nigeria is _______

options.text: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress

questions.explanation: The Nigerian national motto is 'Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress'.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: How many geopolitical zones are in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 6 geopolitical zones: North-Central, North-East, North-West, South-East, South-South, and South-West.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The official language of Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: English is the official language, inherited from British colonial rule. It is used for government, business, and education.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The three major ethnic groups in Nigeria are _______
questions.explanation: The three major ethnic groups are Hausa (mainly in the North), Yoruba (mainly in the South-West), and Igbo (mainly in the South-East).

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Democracy means government of the people, by the people, _______
questions.explanation: This is Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address definition (1863), the most famous definition of democracy in the world.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: One feature of democracy is _______
questions.explanation: Free and fair elections are a defining feature of democracy. Citizens must be able to choose their leaders peacefully.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A system of government where power is shared between central and state governments is called _______
questions.explanation: Federalism divides power between the central (federal) government and state governments. Nigeria operates a federal system.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The separation of powers divides government into _______
questions.explanation: The three arms are the Legislature (makes laws), the Executive (implements laws), and the Judiciary (interprets laws). The principle prevents abuse of power.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Universal suffrage means _______

options.text: every adult has the right to vote

questions.explanation: Universal suffrage is the right of all adult citizens (18 and above in Nigeria) to vote, regardless of gender, education, or wealth.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to life means _______

options.text: no one should be killed unlawfully
people can decide when to die

questions.explanation: The right to life is the most fundamental human right. It is protected by Section 33 of the Nigerian Constitution.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to fair hearing is guaranteed in _______
questions.explanation: Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution guarantees fair hearing, including being heard by a competent court within a reasonable time.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Right to dignity of human person is protected in _______
questions.explanation: Section 34 protects dignity of human person — no one shall be subjected to torture, inhuman or degrading treatment.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Freedom of movement is a _______
questions.explanation: Freedom of movement is enshrined in Section 41 of the Constitution. Every citizen can move freely throughout Nigeria.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Which organization promotes human rights worldwide?
questions.explanation: The United Nations (UN), through the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), is the global body that promotes and protects human rights.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A public servant is someone who _______
questions.explanation: A public servant is any person employed by the government (federal, state, or local) to serve the public.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A traffic warden is a _______
questions.explanation: A traffic warden is a public servant employed by the government to enforce traffic laws and direct traffic on public roads.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Service to the community is the responsibility of _______
questions.explanation: Service to the community is a civic responsibility of every citizen, not just government officials.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was established in _______
questions.explanation: NYSC was established in 1973 to promote national unity, with graduates serving one year outside their state of origin.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Loss of citizenship is called _______
questions.explanation: Renunciation is the voluntary act of giving up one's citizenship. Citizenship can also be revoked in cases of fraud during naturalization.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A person who is not a citizen of any country is called _______
questions.explanation: A stateless person has no nationality. Aliens are foreigners in a country. Refugees are people fleeing persecution. Expatriates are citizens living abroad.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Who is a citizen by birth in Nigeria?

options.text: A child born to Nigerian parents
A child born to foreign parents in Nigeria
A child born in a Nigerian hospital to tourists

questions.explanation: By Section 25 of the 1999 Constitution, citizenship by birth requires that either parent or grandparent be a citizen of Nigeria.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The age at which a person can vote in Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution (Section 126) gives Nigerian citizens 18 years and above the right to vote in elections.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A national identity card is a proof of _______
questions.explanation: The National Identity Card (issued by NIMC) proves a person's identity and citizenship for official purposes.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Constitution is divided into _______ chapters
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria has 8 chapters, plus schedules, covering different aspects of governance and fundamental rights.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The chapter that contains fundamental human rights in the 1999 Constitution is Chapter _______
questions.explanation: Chapter IV (Sections 33-46) of the 1999 Constitution contains the Fundamental Rights, including right to life, liberty, fair hearing, etc.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Constitution can only be amended by _______

options.text: the National Assembly with presidential assent

questions.explanation: Constitutional amendments require two-thirds majority in both Senate and House of Representatives, then presidential assent.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Constitution guarantees all these rights EXCEPT _______
questions.explanation: The Constitution does not guarantee any right to commit crimes. All other listed rights are constitutionally protected.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: An independent judiciary is essential for _______
questions.explanation: An independent judiciary is essential to ensure laws are applied fairly and the rule of law is maintained.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The highest court in Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the highest court in Nigeria's judicial hierarchy, located in Abuja. Its decisions are final.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The concept that no one is above the law is called _______
questions.explanation: Rule of law means every person, including government officials, is subject to and accountable under the law.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Free and fair elections are a feature of _______
questions.explanation: Free and fair elections, with universal suffrage, are a defining feature of democracy.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A government formed by the people is called _______
questions.explanation: Democracy is government of the people. Monarchy is rule by a king/queen. Oligarchy is rule by a few. Aristocracy is rule by the nobility.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right of citizens to choose their leaders is called _______
questions.explanation: Franchise is the right to vote. Universal franchise means all adult citizens can vote regardless of wealth, gender, or class.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A system of government where power is held by one person is called _______
questions.explanation: Autocracy is rule by one person with absolute power. Democracy is rule by the people. Federation is shared power. Republic is state where power rests with citizens.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: National Day in Nigeria is celebrated on _______
questions.explanation: Independence Day is celebrated on October 1st each year, marking Nigeria's independence from British colonial rule in 1960.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Democracy Day in Nigeria is celebrated on _______
questions.explanation: Democracy Day is celebrated on June 12, marking the annulled 1993 election won by M.K.O. Abiola. It was changed from May 29 to June 12 in 2018.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Workers' Day (May Day) in Nigeria is celebrated on _______
questions.explanation: International Workers' Day is celebrated globally on May 1. It recognizes workers' contributions and the labour movement.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian flag was designed by _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian flag was designed by Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi, a student, in 1959 for the country's independence.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A public servant must be _______ in the discharge of his duties
questions.explanation: Public servants are expected to be honest, diligent, fair, and serve the public interest. Corruption and partiality violate public service rules.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The body that investigates corruption in Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC) investigate corruption cases in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A tax is a _______ payment to government
questions.explanation: Tax is a compulsory financial charge imposed by government on persons, businesses, or transactions to fund public expenditure.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to life means that no one should be _______ unlawfully
questions.explanation: Section 33(1) of the Constitution: 'Every person has a right to life, and no one shall be deprived intentionally of his life, save in execution of the sentence of a court in respect of a criminal offence...'

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN in _______
questions.explanation: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the UN General Assembly on December 10, 1948. December 10 is now International Human Rights Day.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Every accused person has the right to a _______ hearing
questions.explanation: Section 36 of the Constitution guarantees fair hearing within a reasonable time by an independent and impartial court.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) is _______
questions.explanation: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) is Abuja, which became Nigeria's capital on December 12, 1991, replacing Lagos.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The head of the Nigerian Armed Forces is the _______
questions.explanation: By the Constitution, the President is the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. The Chief of Defence Staff is the highest military officer.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian police is controlled by the _______
questions.explanation: The Inspector General of Police (IGP) heads the Nigeria Police Force, which operates under the federal government.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a civic responsibility of a citizen?
questions.explanation: Voting in elections is a key civic responsibility. The other three are illegal acts, not responsibilities.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to own property is a _______ right
questions.explanation: The right to own property (acquire and own immovable property anywhere in Nigeria) is a fundamental right under Section 43 of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The best way to resolve conflict is through _______
questions.explanation: Peaceful dialogue, negotiation, mediation, and arbitration are the best ways to resolve conflicts. Violence only escalates problems.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The agency responsible for maintaining peace and order in Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Police Force is primarily responsible for maintaining law and order. The Army is for external defense but can be called in for internal security.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first constitution of Nigeria was the _______
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was the first written constitution for Nigeria, introduced by Sir Hugh Clifford.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 introduced _______ in Nigeria
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 established true federalism in Nigeria with regional governments and a federal structure.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Independence Constitution of 1960 was a(n) _______ constitution
questions.explanation: The 1960 Independence Constitution established a Westminster-style parliamentary system with a Prime Minister as head of government.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The 1979 Constitution introduced the _______ system of government
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution introduced the American-style presidential system, replacing the parliamentary system of the 1st and 2nd Republics.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The 1999 Constitution is the current _______ of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution is Nigeria's current grundnorm — the supreme law from which all other laws derive their validity.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian National Anthem was first adopted in _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria's first national anthem 'Nigeria, We Hail Thee' was adopted in 1960 at independence. It was replaced in 1978 by 'Arise, O Compatriots'.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The second National Anthem 'Arise, O Compatriots' was adopted in _______
questions.explanation: 'Arise, O Compatriots' was adopted in 1978 during military rule. In 2024, Nigeria returned to the old 'Nigeria, We Hail Thee' anthem.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian coat of arms has _______ as the motto

options.text: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress

questions.explanation: The Nigerian coat of arms has a black shield, two white horses (or yanks), an eagle, and the green and white bands with the motto 'Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress'.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The colour of the Nigerian flag represents _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian flag: green represents agriculture, natural wealth, and the lush vegetation. White represents peace and unity.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Inspector General of Police is appointed by the _______
questions.explanation: The Inspector General of Police (IGP) is appointed by the President on the advice of the Nigeria Police Council.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A by-election is conducted to fill a seat that has become _______
questions.explanation: A by-election is a special election held to fill a vacant seat in a legislature, e.g., when a member dies, resigns, or is disqualified.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A vote of no confidence is used to _______ the government
questions.explanation: A vote of no confidence is a parliamentary procedure where members vote to express their lack of support for the government.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: An opposition party is the political party that _______

options.text: did not win the election but is the second largest

questions.explanation: The opposition is the party/parties that did not form the government. They play a key role in holding the government accountable in a democracy.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The tenure of the President of Nigeria is _______ years
questions.explanation: The presidential tenure in Nigeria is 4 years per term, with a maximum of two terms (8 years total).

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The tenure of state governors is _______
questions.explanation: State governors serve 4-year terms and can be re-elected for a maximum of two terms (8 years total), same as the President.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The national electoral body in Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: INEC (Independent National Electoral Commission) is the body constitutionally empowered to conduct all elections in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The chairman of INEC is appointed by the _______
questions.explanation: The INEC Chairman is appointed by the President, subject to confirmation by the Senate.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The minimum number of states that must be created by the National Assembly to form a new state is _______
questions.explanation: To create a new state, the proposal must be supported by at least two-thirds majority of members of the National Assembly, and the state must have a referendum.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigeria's six geopolitical zones are mainly used for _______
questions.explanation: The six geopolitical zones (North-Central, North-East, North-West, South-East, South-South, South-West) are used for administrative convenience and political organization, e.g., power rotation.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A Nigerian citizen can hold dual citizenship with another country if _______
questions.explanation: Section 28 of the Constitution allows dual citizenship — a Nigerian can hold citizenship of another country. The other country must also permit dual citizenship.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A 'ward' in Nigerian local government is a _______
questions.explanation: A ward is the smallest administrative unit in Nigeria's local government system. Each ward has a councillor representing the people.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The three arms of government in Nigeria are _______
questions.explanation: The three arms are Legislative (makes laws), Executive (implements laws), and Judiciary (interprets laws). The principle of separation of powers prevents abuse.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Civil War (1967-1970) was triggered by _______
questions.explanation: The civil war was triggered by the declaration of the Republic of Biafra by the Eastern Region under Lt. Col. Ojukwu on May 30, 1967, after political tensions.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Who led the federal side during the Nigerian Civil War?
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon was the Head of State and led the federal side during the 1967-1970 civil war. He was 31 years old when he became Head of State.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was established to _______
questions.explanation: NYSC was established in 1973 to promote national unity and integration by posting young graduates to serve in states other than their state of origin for one year.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The National Pledge in Nigeria is recited in _______
questions.explanation: The National Pledge is recited in schools (especially at assemblies) and at official functions. It expresses loyalty to the nation.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The civil defence corps is responsible for _______
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) is responsible for disaster management, emergency response, and protecting critical infrastructure.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) is responsible for _______
questions.explanation: The FRSC manages traffic, enforces road safety laws, educates drivers and pedestrians, and reduces road accidents.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: EFCC stands for _______
questions.explanation: EFCC (Economic and Financial Crimes Commission) was established in 2003 to investigate and prosecute financial crimes like fraud, money laundering, and corruption.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: ICPC stands for _______
questions.explanation: ICPC (Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission) was established in 2000 to combat corruption in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A government by the rich is called _______
questions.explanation: Plutocracy is government by the wealthy. Examples: ancient Sparta, some modern critics of the US. Aristocracy is rule by the nobility

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A government by the few is called _______
questions.explanation: Oligarchy is rule by a small group of people (often the wealthy or powerful). Modern examples: some political systems dominated by a few families

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A government by religious leaders is called _______
questions.explanation: Theocracy is rule by religious leaders or by divine guidance. Examples: Iran, Vatican City, ancient Egypt under the Pharaohs (considered a god)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A government by a single ruler is called _______
questions.explanation: Autocracy = rule by one person with absolute power. Monarchy = rule by a king/queen (often hereditary)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A government in which power is held by the people is called _______
questions.explanation: Democracy = government by the people. From Greek 'demos' (people) + 'kratos' (rule)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: An absolute monarchy is one in which the king/queen has _______ power
questions.explanation: In an absolute monarchy, the monarch has unlimited power. Examples: Saudi Arabia, Brunei, Oman

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A constitutional monarchy is one in which the monarch's power is limited by _______
questions.explanation: In a constitutional monarchy, the monarch's power is limited by a constitution and laws. Examples: UK, Japan, Spain, Sweden

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A unitary state has _______
questions.explanation: A unitary state has a strong central government. Power may be delegated to regions but can be taken back. Examples: France, Japan, Kenya

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A federal state has _______

options.text: power divided between central and regional governments

questions.explanation: A federal state divides power constitutionally between central and regional governments. Examples: Nigeria, USA, India, Brazil

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A confederal state has _______

options.text: a weak central government with strong regional governments

questions.explanation: A confederation has a weak central authority with strong regional governments. Examples: EU, early USA under Articles of Confederation

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Universal suffrage means _______
questions.explanation: Universal suffrage = all adult citizens (typically 18+) can vote, regardless of gender, wealth, education, or class. Achieved progressively worldwide

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Plural suffrage means _______

options.text: voting rights based on property, education, or tax payment

questions.explanation: Plural suffrage = voting rights based on property, education, or tax payment (used historically in some countries, now largely abandoned)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to vote is called _______
questions.explanation: Franchise or suffrage = the right to vote in public elections. The terms are often used interchangeably

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: An electoral system in which the candidate with the most votes wins is called _______
questions.explanation: First-past-the-post (FPTP) is the simplest system: the candidate with the most votes wins. Used in Nigeria, UK, US, Canada

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Proportional representation (PR) means _______

options.text: seats are allocated based on the percentage of votes
the candidate with most votes wins

questions.explanation: PR allocates seats in proportion to votes received. Used in many European countries. Helps smaller parties get representation

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A coalition government is formed when _______

options.text: no single party wins a majority

questions.explanation: Coalition = alliance of two or more parties to form a government, usually when no single party has a majority

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A hung parliament occurs when _______

options.text: no party has a clear majority

questions.explanation: Hung parliament = no party has a clear majority. The largest party must form a coalition or seek a vote of confidence

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A vote of no confidence is when parliament _______

options.text: votes to show disapproval of the government

questions.explanation: Vote of no confidence = parliament votes to express lack of confidence in the government. If passed, the government must resign or call new elections

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A by-election is held to _______

options.text: fill a vacant seat between general elections

questions.explanation: By-election = special election to fill a single vacant seat between general elections, e.g., when a member dies, resigns, or is disqualified

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A referendum is _______

options.text: a direct vote by citizens on a specific issue

questions.explanation: Referendum = direct vote by citizens on a specific issue, policy, or law. The result is binding. Examples: Brexit (UK, 2016), same-sex marriage (Ireland, 2015)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: An initiative is _______
questions.explanation: Initiative = a citizen-proposed law or amendment, usually requiring a certain number of signatures. Used in some US states and Switzerland

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A plebiscite is _______

options.text: a popular vote on a territorial or sovereignty issue

questions.explanation: Plebiscite = direct vote by citizens on a major issue, often territorial or sovereignty-related. Example: 1961 plebiscite in British Cameroons to join Cameroon or Nigeria

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Gerrymandering is the manipulation of _______ for political advantage
questions.explanation: Gerrymandering = manipulation of electoral district boundaries to favor one party or group. Common in US, less common in Nigeria

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The separation of powers was first theorized by _______
questions.explanation: Charles-Louis de Secondat, Baron de Montesquieu, in 'The Spirit of the Laws' (1748), proposed the separation of legislative, executive, and judicial powers

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Checks and balances are designed to _______

options.text: prevent any one branch from becoming too powerful

questions.explanation: Checks and balances = each branch of government can limit the powers of the others, preventing tyranny. Designed by the Framers of the US Constitution

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The rule of law means _______

options.text: everyone is subject to the law, including rulers
the president is above the law

questions.explanation: Rule of law = principle that all persons, institutions, and entities are accountable to laws that are publicly disclosed, equally enforced, and independently adjudicated

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Due process of law means _______

options.text: the government must follow fair procedures before depriving a person of life, liberty, or property
the military is exempt from laws

questions.explanation: Due process = fair procedures through which the government must act. Includes notice, opportunity to be heard, and impartial tribunal. Embedded in Section 36 of the Nigerian Constitution

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Habeas corpus means _______

options.text: a person must be brought before a court to determine if their detention is lawful
the police can arrest without warrant
the military can hold suspects indefinitely

questions.explanation: Habeas corpus = 'you shall have the body' — a legal action requiring a person under arrest to be brought before a judge to decide if the detention is lawful. Fundamental right

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The independence of the judiciary means _______

options.text: judges can make decisions free from political pressure

questions.explanation: Judicial independence = judges can make decisions based on law and evidence, free from political or other improper pressure. Essential for rule of law

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The impeachment process is used to _______

options.text: remove a public official for misconduct

questions.explanation: Impeachment = formal process of charging a public official with misconduct, which can lead to their removal from office. Used in Nigeria, US, Brazil, etc.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Censorship is the suppression of _______
questions.explanation: Censorship = suppression of speech, writing, images, or other forms of expression by governments, media organizations, or other controlling bodies. Often controversial in democracies

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Freedom of speech is the right to _______
questions.explanation: Freedom of speech = right to express ideas and opinions without government censorship, subject to reasonable limits (e.g., no incitement to violence, defamation)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A defector is someone who _______

options.text: leaves one country or political group to join another

questions.explanation: Defector = person who leaves their country or political group to join another, often for political reasons. Examples: Soviet defectors to the West during the Cold War

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Exile is _______

options.text: being away from one's home country, often as punishment

questions.explanation: Exile = being barred from one's home country, often as punishment. Voluntary exile is leaving to avoid persecution. Many African leaders have been in exile

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Asylum is _______

options.text: protection given by a country to a foreigner fleeing persecution

questions.explanation: Asylum = protection given by a country to a person fleeing persecution in their own country. Recognized in international law. The 1951 Refugee Convention is the key document

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: A refugee is a person who _______

options.text: fled their country due to war, persecution, or natural disaster

questions.explanation: Refugee = person who has fled their home country due to well-founded fear of persecution, war, or violence. Legally distinct from migrant or asylum seeker

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) was established in _______
questions.explanation: The UNHCR was established in 1950 by the UN General Assembly to lead and coordinate international action for refugees worldwide. Won Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted in _______
questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly on December 10, 1948 in Paris. December 10 is now International Human Rights Day

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The 1951 Refugee Convention defines who is a _______
questions.explanation: The 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees defines a refugee as someone with well-founded fear of persecution on grounds of race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Internally displaced persons (IDPs) are people who _______

options.text: fled their homes but remain within their country

questions.explanation: IDPs = people forced to flee their homes due to conflict, persecution, or disaster, but who have not crossed an international border. Distinct from refugees. Nigeria has many IDPs from Boko Haram and farmer-herder conflicts

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to education is a _______ right
questions.explanation: Education is a fundamental human right, recognized in the UDHR (Article 26) and many national constitutions, including Nigeria. Free and compulsory primary education is a global standard

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to health is a _______ right
questions.explanation: Health is a fundamental human right, recognized in the WHO Constitution and the UDHR. Access to healthcare is a key social right

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to work is a _______ right
questions.explanation: The right to work is recognized in the UDHR (Article 23). Includes the right to free choice of employment, just conditions, and protection against unemployment

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to food is a _______ right
questions.explanation: The right to adequate food is a fundamental human right, recognized in the ICESCR (Article 11). Governments have an obligation to ensure access to food for their citizens

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The right to clean water is recognized in the _______
questions.explanation: Access to clean water and sanitation is recognized in UN SDG 6 and the ICESCR. Increasingly treated as a fundamental human right

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Sustainable development is development that _______

options.text: meets present needs without compromising future generations

questions.explanation: Sustainable development = development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. The Brundtland Report definition (1987)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Brundtland Report on sustainable development was published in _______
questions.explanation: The Brundtland Report (Our Common Future) was published in 1987 by the World Commission on Environment and Development. Defined sustainable development as we know it

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Rio Earth Summit was held in _______
questions.explanation: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), known as the Rio Earth Summit, was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992. Led to Agenda 21, the UNFCCC, and the Convention on Biological Diversity

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Paris Agreement on climate change was signed in _______
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement was signed in 2015 at COP21. Aims to limit global warming to well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C, compared to pre-industrial levels

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in _______
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in 1997 (entered into force 2005). First international treaty to set binding targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The United Nations was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The United Nations (UN) was founded on October 24, 1945, after World War II, replacing the League of Nations. October 24 is United Nations Day

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights has _______ articles
questions.explanation: The UDHR has 30 articles. The first 21 cover civil and political rights; articles 22-27 cover economic, social, and cultural rights; articles 28-30 cover general duties and limitations

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights was adopted in _______
questions.explanation: The African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights (Banjul Charter) was adopted in 1981 by the OAU (now AU) in Nairobi, Kenya

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first democratically elected president of South Africa was _______
questions.explanation: Nelson Mandela was the first democratically elected president of South Africa in 1994, after the end of apartheid. He served until 1999

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Apartheid in South Africa ended in _______
questions.explanation: Apartheid officially ended in 1994 with the first democratic elections. Nelson Mandela was released from prison in 1990 and negotiations led to the end of apartheid

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The OAU was founded in 1963 by 32 African states in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It was replaced by the African Union (AU) in 2002

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The African Union (AU) was founded in _______ to replace the OAU
questions.explanation: The African Union was founded in 2002 in Durban, South Africa, replacing the OAU. The AU has more powers than the OAU, including the ability to intervene in member states in cases of genocide, war crimes, etc.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The AU headquarters is in _______
questions.explanation: The African Union (AU) has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The ECOWAS Treaty was signed in _______
questions.explanation: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) was founded on May 28, 1975, by the Treaty of Lagos. Nigeria is a founding member

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: ECOWAS headquarters is in _______
questions.explanation: ECOWAS headquarters is in Abuja, Nigeria, established in 1977

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The ECOWAS standby force (ESF) was established to _______

options.text: respond to crises in member states

questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Standby Force is a multinational peacekeeping force, comprising military, police, and civilian components from member states, for rapid response to crises

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigerian foreign policy is based on the principles of _______

options.text: non-alignment, respect for sovereignty, and African unity

questions.explanation: Nigeria's foreign policy principles include: non-alignment in the Cold War era, respect for sovereign equality, non-interference, peaceful settlement of disputes, respect for human rights, and African unity

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Commonwealth of Nations was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The modern Commonwealth was founded in 1949 with the London Declaration. The British Commonwealth of Nations became simply the Commonwealth of Nations. Nigeria joined in 1960

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: OPEC (Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: OPEC was founded on September 14, 1960, in Baghdad, Iraq, by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela. Nigeria joined in 1971

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The AU's peacekeeping body is called _______
questions.explanation: The African Standby Force (ASF) is the AU's peacekeeping body, comprising five regional brigades (one per AU region)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The UN Security Council has _______ permanent members
questions.explanation: The UN Security Council has 5 permanent members (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) and 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms. Total: 15

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The UN General Assembly has _______ members
questions.explanation: The UN General Assembly has 193 member states (as of 2023), each with one vote. Decisions on important issues require a two-thirds majority

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigeria was admitted to the UN in _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria was admitted to the UN on October 7, 1960, the same year of independence

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigeria was admitted to the Commonwealth in _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria was admitted to the Commonwealth in 1960 at independence

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth in _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth in 1995 under General Sani Abacha's regime, due to human rights abuses and the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigeria was readmitted to the Commonwealth in _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria was readmitted to the Commonwealth in 1999, with the restoration of democratic rule under President Obasanjo

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The concept of African Renaissance was popularized by _______
questions.explanation: The concept of African Renaissance was popularized by Thabo Mbeki (former South African president) in the 1990s-2000s, referring to a renewal of African identity, economy, and politics

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD) was established in _______
questions.explanation: NEPAD was established in 2001 by African leaders (Thabo Mbeki, Olusegun Obasanjo, Abdoulaye Wade) to promote sustainable development and address Africa's challenges

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian Permanent Representative to the UN was _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria's first Permanent Representative to the UN was appointed in 1960. Several early diplomats held the position

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Commonwealth Charter was adopted in _______
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth Charter was adopted by the Queen in 2012, setting out the values and principles of the Commonwealth

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) headquarters is in _______
questions.explanation: UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya. The UN Office in Nairobi is the only major UN headquarters in the Global South

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: UNESCO (UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: UNESCO was founded on November 16, 1945, in London. Headquarters: Paris, France. Mission: to promote peace through international cooperation in education, science, and culture

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: UNESCO headquarters is in _______
questions.explanation: UNESCO headquarters is in Paris, France

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The World Health Organization (WHO) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The WHO was founded on April 7, 1948 (World Health Day). Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: UNICEF was founded in 1946 to help children in post-WWII Europe. Now works globally. Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is in _______
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the UN, is in The Hague, Netherlands. Established in 1945

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The International Criminal Court (ICC) is in _______
questions.explanation: The International Criminal Court (ICC), established by the Rome Statute in 2002, is in The Hague, Netherlands. Prosecutes genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Rome Statute established the ICC in _______
questions.explanation: The Rome Statute was adopted in 1998 and entered into force on July 1, 2002. Nigeria is a State Party

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigeria signed the Rome Statute in _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria signed the Rome Statute (creating the ICC) in 2000 and ratified in 2002

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The ECOWAS Court of Justice is in _______
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Court of Justice is in Abuja, Nigeria

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights is in _______
questions.explanation: The African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights is in Arusha, Tanzania. Established by a protocol to the African Charter in 2006

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The International Labour Organization (ILO) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The ILO was founded in 1919 as part of the League of Nations. It became a UN specialized agency in 1946. Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: ILO headquarters is in _______
questions.explanation: The ILO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The IMF was founded in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference. Headquarters: Washington D.C., USA

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The World Bank was established in _______
questions.explanation: The World Bank was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference. Headquarters: Washington D.C., USA. Initially to help rebuild post-WWII Europe

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The World Trade Organization (WTO) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The WTO was founded on January 1, 1995, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT, 1947). Headquarters: Geneva

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The G77 (Group of 77) was formed in _______
questions.explanation: The Group of 77 was formed on June 15, 1964, by 77 developing countries to promote collective economic interests. Now has 134 members

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: NAM was founded in 1961 in Belgrade, Yugoslavia, by India, Egypt, Yugoslavia, Indonesia, and Ghana. Aims to maintain independence from the superpowers during the Cold War

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Nigeria was a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement in _______

options.text: 1964 (and 1961, but Nigeria joined at the 1964 Cairo Conference as a full member)

questions.explanation: Nigeria was a key member of NAM. It formally joined at the 1964 Cairo Conference

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first African country to gain independence was _______
questions.explanation: Ghana (formerly Gold Coast) gained independence on March 6, 1957, the first sub-Saharan African country to do so. Led by Kwame Nkrumah

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Kwame Nkrumah was the first president of _______
questions.explanation: Kwame Nkrumah was the first Prime Minister and first President of Ghana, leading the country to independence in 1957 and beyond

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Liberia gained independence in _______
questions.explanation: Liberia gained independence on July 26, 1847. It was founded in 1822 by the American Colonization Society for freed American slaves. One of the oldest republics in Africa

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Ethiopia was never formally colonized by Europeans, except for a brief Italian occupation in _______
questions.explanation: Ethiopia defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa in 1896. Italy invaded and occupied Ethiopia in 1936-1941, but Ethiopian resistance (the Arbegnoch) helped defeat Italian fascism

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Mau Mau uprising was a rebellion in _______
questions.explanation: The Mau Mau uprising was a rebellion against British colonial rule in Kenya, primarily by the Kikuyu people, 1952-1960. Led to Kenyan independence in 1963

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Sharpeville Massacre occurred in _______
questions.explanation: The Sharpeville Massacre occurred on March 21, 1960, in Sharpeville, South Africa, when police killed 69 anti-apartheid protesters. A turning point in the anti-apartheid movement

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Steve Biko was a leader of the _______ movement in South Africa
questions.explanation: Steve Biko (1946-1977) was the founder of the Black Consciousness Movement (BCM) in South Africa. He was murdered in police custody in 1977

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Pan-African Congress of 1945 was held in _______
questions.explanation: The Fifth Pan-African Congress was held in Manchester, UK, in October 1945. Organized by George Padmore and W.E.B. Du Bois, with Kwame Nkrumah as joint secretary. It set the stage for African independence movements

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Kwame Nkrumah's political philosophy was _______
questions.explanation: Nkrumah advocated African socialism and Pan-Africanism. He believed in the unity of African states and that socialism was the path to development. Famous for 'Seek ye first the political kingdom'

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was founded by _______

options.text: Haile Selassie of Ethiopia and other African leaders

questions.explanation: The OAU was founded on May 25, 1963, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, by 32 heads of state. The driving force was Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first OAU Secretary-General was _______
questions.explanation: Diallo Telli of Guinea was the first Secretary-General of the OAU, serving from 1964 to 1972

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) Liberation Committee was based in _______
questions.explanation: The OAU Liberation Committee was based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, coordinating support for liberation movements in southern Africa

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian civil war (Biafran War) was triggered by the assassination of _______

options.text: Several Northern leaders in the 1966 coup (Tafawa Balewa, Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Ahmadu Bello)

questions.explanation: The 1966 counter-coup that brought Gowon to power was in part a response to the January 1966 coup, which killed several Northern and Western leaders. The killings of Ahmadu Bello, Tafawa Balewa, and others inflamed ethnic tensions

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Aburi Accord attempted to resolve the crisis that led to the _______
questions.explanation: The Aburi Accord (Ghana, 1967) attempted to resolve the constitutional crisis between the federal government and the Eastern Region. Its failure contributed to the declaration of Biafra

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The leader of Biafra during the civil war was _______
questions.explanation: Lt. Col. Emeka Odumegwu Ojukwu was the leader of Biafra (1967-1970). He led the secession and the war effort. After the war, he went into exile, returning in 1982

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The slogan 'No victor, no vanquished' was used by _______

options.text: General Yakubu Gowon after the civil war (1970)

questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon used the slogan 'No victor, no vanquished' in his reconciliation speech on January 15, 1970, after the Biafran surrender. Aimed to promote healing

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The '3Rs' of Gowon's post-war policy were _______
questions.explanation: Gowon's '3Rs' policy: Reconciliation, Reconstruction, and Rehabilitation. Aimed to heal the divisions of the civil war

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Head of State to give a 'Handshake Across the Niger' was _______

options.text: Shehu Shagari (1979, after the Second Republic began) — but the term was popularized by Murtala Mohammed's regime in 1976
