questions.prompt: The PDP was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The People's Democratic Party (PDP) was founded in 1998, ahead of the 1999 elections. The PDP won the 1999, 2003, and 2007 elections, losing to APC in 2015

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The APC (All Progressives Congress) was founded in _______
questions.explanation: The All Progressives Congress (APC) was founded in February 2013, through a merger of several opposition parties. It won the 2015 presidential election with Muhammadu Buhari

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Muhammadu Buhari first became Head of State through a coup in _______
questions.explanation: Muhammadu Buhari first came to power through a military coup on December 31, 1983, overthrowing the Second Republic. He was overthrown by Babangida in 1985

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Buhari returned to power as a civilian president in _______
questions.explanation: Muhammadu Buhari returned to power as a democratically elected president in 2015, on the APC platform. He was re-elected in 2019 and lost in 2023 to Bola Tinubu

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Bola Tinubu became President of Nigeria in _______
questions.explanation: Bola Tinubu was inaugurated as President of Nigeria on May 29, 2023, succeeding Muhammadu Buhari

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Goodluck Jonathan was President from _______
questions.explanation: Goodluck Jonathan became Acting President in 2010 after Yar'Adua's death, then President. He won election in 2011 and served until 2015

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: Umaru Yar'Adua was President from _______
questions.explanation: Umaru Yar'Adua was President from 2007 to 2010, when he died in office. Jonathan then took over

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The longest-serving civilian president of Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Olusegun Obasanjo served as civilian president for 8 years (1999-2007). Tinubu is also serving since 2023

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The shortest-serving Head of State was _______
questions.explanation: Ernest Shonekan served as interim Head of State from August 26 to November 17, 1993 (about 3 months), before Sani Abacha took over in a coup

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first military Head of State from outside the North was _______
questions.explanation: General J.T.U. Aguiyi-Ironsi was the first military Head of State (1966) and the first from the East (Igbo). His regime was short-lived due to the counter-coup

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first military Head of State from the Middle Belt was _______
questions.explanation: General Murtala Mohammed was from the Middle Belt (Kano, but of Kanuri descent — his family is from the Middle Belt/North-East border). He was assassinated in 1976

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Abacha regime is associated with _______
questions.explanation: General Sani Abacha's regime (1993-1998) is associated with severe human rights abuses, corruption (an estimated $3-5 billion stolen), and the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa in 1995

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be awarded the Nobel Prize was _______
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, the first African and first Nigerian to win a Nobel

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian who wrote Things Fall Apart is _______
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe (1930-2013) wrote Things Fall Apart (1958), one of the most famous African novels. He was nominated for the Nobel Prize multiple times

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian author who wrote The Man Died is _______
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka wrote The Man Died: Prison Notes (1972), a memoir of his time in prison during the civil war. He also wrote A Dance of the Forests, The Lion and the Jewel, etc.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian author who won the Booker Prize is _______

options.text: Ben Okri (1991 for The Famished Road)

questions.explanation: Ben Okri won the Booker Prize in 1991 for The Famished Road. He is the only Nigerian to win the Booker

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian female to win the CNN African of the Year is _______

options.text: Several — including Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma (not Nigerian), but in Nigeria, no single female has won in some years

questions.explanation: Various Nigerian women have won recognition. The CNN African of the Year is given annually and includes various Nigerians

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The current Director-General of the WTO is _______
questions.explanation: Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the first African and first woman Director-General of the WTO in March 2021. She is also a former Nigerian Finance Minister

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be a Vice President of the World Bank is _______

options.text: Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (she was Managing Director, not VP)

questions.explanation: Several Nigerians have held senior positions at the World Bank. Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala was a Managing Director, not Vice President

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be a UN Under-Secretary-General is _______

options.text: Several, including Amina J. Mohammed (current Deputy Secretary-General)

questions.explanation: Amina J. Mohammed, former Nigerian Minister of Environment, is the current UN Deputy Secretary-General. Several Nigerians have held UN positions

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be President of the UN General Assembly was _______

options.text: No Nigerian has served as President of the UNGA

questions.explanation: No Nigerian has served as President of the UN General Assembly (as of 2024). Several Africans have, including former Tanzanian and Ugandan leaders

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be a member of the International Court of Justice is _______
questions.explanation: Taslim Olawale Elias, former Chief Justice of Nigeria, was a judge at the International Court of Justice from 1982 to 1991. He was also a legal scholar of note

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian city of Lagos was founded by _______

options.text: The Portuguese (15th-17th century) / developed by the British

questions.explanation: Lagos was originally a Yoruba settlement (Eko) and was visited by the Portuguese in the 15th century. It became a major slave port. The British annexed it in 1861

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The city of Abuja was officially designated as Nigeria's capital by _______
questions.explanation: The decision to move the capital to Abuja was made in 1976 by the Murtala Mohammed regime, based on a panel's recommendation. The move was completed on December 12, 1991

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Aguda panel on the new capital was led by _______
questions.explanation: Justice Akinola Aguda led the panel that recommended Abuja as the site for the new federal capital, in 1975-1976

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first indigenous mayor of Lagos was _______
questions.explanation: Akinsanya Coker was the first indigenous mayor of Lagos (1950s)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to become a judge of the World Court (ICJ) was _______
questions.explanation: Taslim Olawale Elias was a judge of the ICJ from 1982 to 1991. He was also Chief Justice of Nigeria (1972-1975)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first female to head a UN agency is _______

options.text: Several — including WFP, UNESCO, etc. Margaret Chan (WHO) and Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka (UN Women) are notable

questions.explanation: Many women have headed UN agencies. Notable examples: Margaret Chan (WHO, 2006-2017), Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka (UN Women, 2013-2019)

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be Secretary-General of OPEC was _______

options.text: No Nigerian has been OPEC Secretary-General

questions.explanation: Rilwanu Lukman served as OPEC Secretary-General from 1995 to 2000. He was also Nigeria's Foreign Minister and a petroleum industry leader

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first female to serve as Speaker of a Nigerian State House of Assembly was _______
questions.explanation: Various women have served as state legislators and speakers, especially after 1999. Margaret Icheen was one of the early state speakers

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian woman to become a brigadier-general in the Army was _______

options.text: Several — including Stella Ameyo Adadevoh (public health icon, not military); military women have risen to general ranks

questions.explanation: Various Nigerian women have served in the military and risen to senior ranks. Recent appointments include female brigadier-generals in the Army and Air Force

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be a Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) is _______

options.text: Several — including Prof. Adeoye Lambo (psychiatrist), Prof. Wole Soyinka (literature, honorary FRS)

questions.explanation: Prof. Wole Soyinka was elected Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature. Prof. Adeoye Lambo was a Fellow of the Royal College of Psychiatrists. Several other Nigerian scientists have been recognized

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be inducted into the International Swimming Hall of Fame is _______
questions.explanation: No Nigerian has been inducted into the International Swimming Hall of Fame. Nigerian swimmers are emerging but not at this level

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be on the cover of TIME magazine was _______
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka was featured in TIME magazine (cover) in the late 1960s-1980s. Other Nigerians have appeared in TIME including leaders and figures

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be on the cover of Vogue magazine was _______

options.text: Various Nigerian models and figures have been featured

questions.explanation: Several Nigerians have appeared in major fashion magazines. Not specific to one individual

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be awarded a CBE (Commander of the Order of the British Empire) was _______
questions.explanation: Kitoyi Ajasa was the first Nigerian to be knighted (KBE — Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire) in 1929

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to be awarded an honorary doctorate from Oxford was _______
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka was awarded an honorary doctorate from the University of Leeds in 1973. He has received many honorary doctorates from around the world

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian university to be ranked in the top 1000 worldwide was _______
questions.explanation: University of Ibadan (UI), established 1948, was the premier university. It was ranked among the top African universities for many years. The University of Lagos, OAU, and others also feature in rankings

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first private university in Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: Igbinedion University, Okada (owned by the Igbinedion family) was licensed in 1999, one of the first private universities in Nigeria

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to win the Caine Prize for African Writing was _______
questions.explanation: Helon Habila won the inaugural Caine Prize for African Writing in 2001. Several other Nigerians have won the prize since

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to win the Africa Prize for Engineering was _______

options.text: Various — including Nuruddeen Usman, Askwar Hilonga, etc. (Askwar Hilonga is Tanzanian)

questions.explanation: The Royal Academy of Engineering's Africa Prize has been won by several Africans. Various Nigerian engineers have won related awards

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to win the Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation was _______

options.text: Several have won, but no Nigerian has won the specific Africa Prize

questions.explanation: No Nigerian has won the Royal Academy of Engineering's Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation as of my knowledge

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian Nobel Prize in any field was won by _______
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, the first Nigerian (and first African) to win any Nobel Prize

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian who won the Booker Prize in 1991 was _______
questions.explanation: Ben Okri won the Booker Prize in 1991 for The Famished Road. He is the first Nigerian to win the Booker

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The Nigerian who won the Caine Prize in 2001 was _______
questions.explanation: Helon Habila won the Caine Prize in 2001, the inaugural winner

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian woman to be a state governor was _______

options.text: No Nigerian woman has been a state governor

questions.explanation: No Nigerian woman has served as a state governor. Several have served as deputy governors, senators, and other offices. Notably, Aisha Jummai Alhassan was a Minister of Women Affairs

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to head a major UN agency was _______

options.text: Several — including the late Prof. Adeoye Lambo (WHO), Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma (not Nigerian) of AU Commission, Dr. Tedros (Ethiopian)

questions.explanation: Prof. Adeoye Lambo was a Deputy Director-General of WHO. Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala heads the WTO since 2021, the most senior UN-related position held by a Nigerian

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to win a FIFA World Cup was _______

options.text: No Nigerian has won a FIFA World Cup

questions.explanation: No Nigerian has won a FIFA World Cup as a player or coach. Nigeria has participated in several World Cups without winning

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to win an Olympic medal was _______

options.text: No Nigerian had won an Olympic medal until recently — the women's 4x400m relay won bronze at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics

questions.explanation: Nigeria's first Olympic medal was the bronze won by the women's 4x400m relay team at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics. Chioma Ajunwa later won gold in long jump at 1996 Atlanta

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.prompt: The first Nigerian to win an Olympic gold medal was _______

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The brain of a computer is called the _______
questions.explanation: The CPU is the brain of the computer. It executes instructions and processes data, consisting of the Control Unit, Arithmetic Logic Unit, and memory.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device — it allows the user to enter data and commands into the computer. Monitor, printer, and speaker are output devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device — it displays visual information from the computer. Mouse, scanner, and joystick are input devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is both an input and output device?
questions.explanation: A touchscreen can both display (output) information and accept (input) touch commands. Other examples include multifunction printers and network interface cards.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Computer memory is measured in _______
questions.explanation: Memory is measured in bytes (e.g., KB, MB, GB, TB). A byte is typically 8 bits. Computer memory stores data and instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: One byte is equal to _______ bits
questions.explanation: A byte is 8 bits. A bit is the smallest unit of data (0 or 1). Bytes are the basic unit for measuring memory and storage.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The short-term memory of a computer is called _______
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile short-term memory. Data in RAM is lost when the computer is turned off. ROM is permanent memory that holds startup instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The permanent memory of a computer is called _______
questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile memory that permanently stores instructions (e.g., the BIOS). Data is not lost when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The operating system is an example of _______ software
questions.explanation: An operating system (e.g., Windows, macOS, Linux, Android) is system software. It manages hardware and provides services for application software.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Microsoft Word is an example of _______ software
questions.explanation: Microsoft Word is application software — designed for users to perform specific tasks like word processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a web browser?
questions.explanation: Google Chrome is a web browser. Others include Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Safari, and Opera.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Linux is a type of _______
questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source operating system kernel. It is the basis for many distributions like Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A hard disk is used for _______
questions.explanation: A hard disk (HDD or SSD) is used for permanent storage of data, programs, and the operating system.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The printer is an example of a(n) _______ device
questions.explanation: A printer produces a physical (paper) copy of digital data — making it an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of the SMPS in a computer is to _______
questions.explanation: SMPS (Switched-Mode Power Supply) converts AC mains electricity to the low-voltage DC power required by computer components.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The full meaning of WWW is _______
questions.explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web, invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. It is the system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The full meaning of URL is _______
questions.explanation: URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a resource on the web, e.g., https://www.example.com.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: HTML stands for _______
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for creating web pages.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a search engine?
questions.explanation: Google is a search engine — it lets you search the internet for information. Other search engines include Bing, Yahoo, and DuckDuckGo.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: LAN stands for _______
questions.explanation: A LAN (Local Area Network) connects computers in a small geographic area like a school, office, or home. WAN (Wide Area Network) covers larger areas.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The Internet is a _______
questions.explanation: The Internet is a global network of interconnected computers using the TCP/IP protocol suite, allowing communication and resource sharing worldwide.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer virus is a _______
questions.explanation: A computer virus is a malicious program designed to spread and damage data, software, or hardware. Antivirus software protects against them.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a way to protect your computer from viruses?
questions.explanation: Installing and regularly updating antivirus software is a key way to protect against malware. Other good practices include using strong passwords and not opening suspicious emails.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Cyberbullying is _______
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying is the use of digital technology (social media, messaging, etc.) to harass, threaten, or humiliate someone. It is a serious issue, especially among young people.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Pirating software means _______
questions.explanation: Software piracy is the unauthorized copying, distribution, or use of copyrighted software. It is illegal and unethical.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Microsoft PowerPoint is used for _______
questions.explanation: Microsoft PowerPoint is presentation software. It allows users to create slideshows with text, images, and animations.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A spreadsheet is used for _______
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet (like Microsoft Excel) is used for organizing, calculating, and analyzing data in rows and columns.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The intersection of a row and a column in a spreadsheet is called a _______
questions.explanation: A cell is the intersection of a row and a column. Each cell has a unique address (e.g., A1, B5) and can hold data, formulas, or functions.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a database management system?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Access is a database management system. Others include MySQL, Oracle, and PostgreSQL.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The smallest unit of data in a computer is the _______
questions.explanation: A bit (binary digit) is the smallest unit of data — it can be either 0 or 1. Eight bits make one byte.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: RAM stands for _______
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile memory that the CPU uses to store data and instructions while the computer is running. It is much faster than a hard drive but loses data when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: ROM stands for _______
questions.explanation: ROM (Read Only Memory) is non-volatile memory that stores permanent instructions, like the BIOS that boots the computer. Data is not lost when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A modem is used to _______
questions.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital signals to analog for transmission over phone lines or cable, allowing internet connection.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A DVD is an example of _______
questions.explanation: DVD (Digital Versatile Disc) is an optical storage medium. CD, Blu-ray are also optical storage. Hard disks and SSDs are other types.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a computer?
questions.explanation: A mechanical calculator (without electronics) is not a computer. A computer is an electronic device that processes data according to a program.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A network that covers a small area like a school is called _______
questions.explanation: LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small geographic area (a building, school, office). MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers a city. WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large geographic areas.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: WiFi is a _______ technology
questions.explanation: WiFi (Wireless Fidelity) is a wireless networking technology that uses radio waves to provide network connectivity. It is defined by the IEEE 802.11 standards.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of an operating system is to _______
questions.explanation: An operating system (OS) manages the computer's hardware, runs applications, handles files, and provides the user interface. Examples: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Microsoft Excel is used for _______
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet application used for calculations, data analysis, charting, and organizing information in rows and columns.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Python is a popular, easy-to-learn programming language. Other programming languages include Java, C++, JavaScript, and Ruby. Word, Chrome, and Photoshop are applications.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An application that lets you create and edit text documents is called a _______
questions.explanation: A word processor (like Microsoft Word, Google Docs, or LibreOffice Writer) is used to create, edit, format, and print text documents.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Antivirus software is used to _______
questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects, prevents, and removes malicious software (viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware). Examples: Norton, McAfee, Avast, Windows Defender.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The '@' symbol in an email address separates _______

options.text: the first name and last name

questions.explanation: In an email like user@example.com, the @ separates the username (user) from the domain name (example.com) which identifies the mail server.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The protocol used to send email is _______
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send emails. POP3 or IMAP is used to receive emails. HTTP is used for web pages.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A cookie is a _______

options.text: small text file stored by a website in your browser

questions.explanation: A cookie is a small text file that a website stores in your browser to remember information about your visit, like login state or preferences.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The cloud refers to _______

options.text: remote servers accessed via the internet
a type of storage inside a computer

questions.explanation: 'The cloud' refers to remote servers and services accessed via the internet, used for storage (Google Drive, Dropbox), computing, and software delivery.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An IP address is _______

options.text: a unique numerical label for a device on a network

questions.explanation: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a unique numerical label assigned to each device on a network. IPv4 looks like 192.168.1.1; IPv6 is longer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: HTTP stands for _______
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. HTTPS is the secure (encrypted) version.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: SSD stands for _______
questions.explanation: SSD (Solid State Drive) is a storage device that uses flash memory (no moving parts), making it faster, quieter, and more durable than HDDs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The main circuit board of a computer is called the _______
questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main printed circuit board that holds the CPU, memory, expansion slots, and connectors for all other components.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A USB drive is used for _______
questions.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) drives, also called flash drives or thumb drives, are portable storage devices that plug into a USB port.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of a UPS is to _______
questions.explanation: A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) provides battery backup power during electricity outages, allowing the user to save work and shut down safely.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Phishing is a _______

options.text: social engineering attack to steal information

questions.explanation: Phishing is a cyberattack where criminals impersonate legitimate organizations (via email, SMS, websites) to trick victims into revealing personal information like passwords or credit card numbers.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Strong passwords should include _______

options.text: your name and date of birth

questions.explanation: Strong passwords mix uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols, and are at least 8-12 characters long. Avoid personal information or dictionary words.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Copyright protects _______

options.text: original creative works like software, music, books

questions.explanation: Copyright is a legal right that protects original creative works (books, music, software, art). It prevents unauthorized copying or distribution by others.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer hacker is someone who _______

options.text: gains unauthorized access to computer systems

questions.explanation: In common usage, a hacker gains unauthorized access to computer systems. Originally, 'hacker' meant a skilled programmer. Ethical hackers (white hats) help find security vulnerabilities.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer receives data through _______ devices
questions.explanation: Input devices (keyboard, mouse, scanner) are how data and instructions enter the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer produces results through _______ devices
questions.explanation: Output devices (monitor, printer, speaker) display or produce the results of processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The main board of a computer is called the _______
questions.explanation: The motherboard (mainboard) is the main printed circuit board that holds the CPU, memory, and connectors for all other components.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The part of the computer that performs calculations is the _______
questions.explanation: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) is part of the CPU that performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which component stores the operating system and applications?
questions.explanation: The hard disk (HDD) or SSD stores the operating system, applications, and user files permanently.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The brain of the computer is the _______
questions.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) executes instructions and is often called the brain of the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A byte is made up of _______ bits
questions.explanation: A byte = 8 bits. It's the standard unit for measuring memory and storage.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which is larger, a kilobyte or a megabyte?
questions.explanation: 1 Megabyte (MB) = 1,024 Kilobytes (KB). So MB > KB. Order: Bit < Byte < KB < MB < GB < TB

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Microsoft Windows is an example of _______
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system. Other OSes: macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The software used to create documents is called a _______
questions.explanation: A word processor (e.g., MS Word, Google Docs) is used to create, edit, format, and print text documents.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Java is a programming language. Word, Chrome, and Windows are applications or an OS.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: HTML is used to create _______
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of the antivirus is to _______
questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects, prevents, and removes malicious software (malware) like viruses, worms, and trojans.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A printer is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A printer produces a physical (paper) copy of digital data — making it an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A mouse is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A mouse is an input device — it allows the user to point, click, and interact with the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The scanner is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device — it converts physical documents/images into digital form.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The monitor is an _______ device
questions.explanation: A monitor displays visual output from the computer — making it an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Which is a storage device?
questions.explanation: Hard Disk (HDD or SSD) is a storage device. The others are input/output devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: RAM stands for _______
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the computer's short-term, volatile memory. It loses data when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: ROM stands for _______
questions.explanation: ROM is permanent, non-volatile memory used to store firmware like the BIOS. Data is not lost when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Wi-Fi stands for _______
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) is a wireless networking technology that uses radio waves for local area networking.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The function of a modem is to _______

options.text: convert digital signals to analog and vice versa

questions.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital data to analog for transmission over phone/cable lines, and back.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The address of a web page is called a _______
questions.explanation: URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a resource on the web, e.g., https://www.example.com.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: HTTPS is the _______ version of HTTP
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP + SSL/TLS encryption. It protects data sent between browser and server.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The part of the URL that identifies the website domain is the _______
questions.explanation: In https://www.example.com/path, the domain name is 'example.com' (with 'www' as subdomain).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A strong password should be at least _______ characters long
questions.explanation: Strong passwords are typically 8-12+ characters. Longer is better. They mix uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A computer virus is a _______
questions.explanation: A virus is a malicious program that spreads by attaching itself to files. It can damage data, software, or hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Phishing is a form of _______
questions.explanation: Phishing is a social engineering attack that tricks users into revealing personal info (passwords, credit card numbers) via fake emails/websites.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: LAN stands for _______
questions.explanation: LAN covers a small geographic area (office, school, home). WAN covers larger areas (countries, continents).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: WAN stands for _______
questions.explanation: WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large geographic areas, like the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A network that connects computers in a school is an example of _______
questions.explanation: A school network is a LAN. PAN (Personal Area Network) is for personal devices. MAN is city-wide. WAN is global.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The inventor of the World Wide Web is _______
questions.explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The inventor of the computer is considered to be _______
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage (1791-1871) is considered the 'father of the computer' for designing the Analytical Engine, the first mechanical computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The first electronic computer was called _______
questions.explanation: ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer) was the first general-purpose electronic computer, completed in 1945 in the USA.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The founder of Microsoft is _______
questions.explanation: Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in 1975. It is one of the world's largest software companies.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The founder of Apple Inc. is _______

options.text: Steve Jobs (with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne)

questions.explanation: Apple Inc. was co-founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in 1976. Jobs is widely credited as the visionary leader.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The founder of Facebook is _______
questions.explanation: Mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in 2004 while at Harvard University. It is now called Meta Platforms.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Google was founded by _______
questions.explanation: Google was founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin in 1998 while they were PhD students at Stanford University.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An operating system manages _______ resources
questions.explanation: An operating system (OS) manages hardware resources (CPU, memory, storage, devices) and provides services to application software.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The boot process is also called _______
questions.explanation: Booting (bootstrapping) is the process of starting a computer — loading the operating system from storage into memory and initializing hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A kilobyte (KB) is approximately _______ bytes
questions.explanation: 1 KB = 1,024 bytes (binary) or 1,000 bytes (decimal). The binary definition is more common in computing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A megabyte (MB) is approximately _______ KB
questions.explanation: 1 MB = 1,024 KB. Order: Bit < Byte < KB < MB < GB < TB < PB

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A gigabyte (GB) is approximately _______ MB
questions.explanation: 1 GB = 1,024 MB. A typical smartphone has 64-256 GB of storage.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A terabyte (TB) is approximately _______ GB
questions.explanation: 1 TB = 1,024 GB. A typical laptop hard drive is 500 GB to 2 TB.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The main memory of a computer is also called _______
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the main working memory. It's fast but volatile (loses data when power is off).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The capacity of a DVD is approximately _______
questions.explanation: A single-layer DVD holds about 4.7 GB. A dual-layer DVD holds about 8.5 GB. Blu-ray discs hold up to 25-50 GB.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The capacity of a CD is approximately _______
questions.explanation: A standard CD holds about 700 MB of data or 80 minutes of audio.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The capacity of a Blu-ray disc is approximately _______
questions.explanation: Blu-ray discs hold 25 GB (single layer), 50 GB (dual layer), or even 100-128 GB (XL).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A pixel is _______

options.text: the smallest element of a digital image

questions.explanation: A pixel (picture element) is the smallest controllable element of a digital image. More pixels = higher resolution.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Resolution refers to _______

options.text: number of pixels in an image

questions.explanation: Resolution is the number of pixels in an image, e.g., 1920x1080 (Full HD). Higher resolution = sharper, more detailed images.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The most common screen resolution today is _______
questions.explanation: 1920x1080 (Full HD) is the most common. 4K (3840x2160) and 8K are increasingly common. Older standards: VGA, SVGA, XGA.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: RAM is a _______ memory
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile — it loses its contents when power is turned off. It's used for temporary data and running programs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: ROM is a _______ memory
questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile — it retains data without power. It contains firmware like the BIOS, which boots the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Cache memory is _______ than RAM
questions.explanation: Cache is a small, very fast memory that stores frequently used data for quick access by the CPU. It's faster but smaller than RAM.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The CPU's clock speed is measured in _______
questions.explanation: CPU clock speed is measured in Hertz (cycles per second). Modern CPUs are 2-5 GHz (gigahertz = billion cycles per second).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A dual-core processor has _______ cores
questions.explanation: Dual-core means 2 cores. Quad-core = 4 cores. Octa-core = 8 cores. More cores = better multitasking.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A graphics card is used for _______
questions.explanation: A graphics card (GPU) is specialized hardware for rendering images, video, and animations. Essential for gaming, video editing, 3D modeling.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: A network interface card (NIC) connects a computer to _______
questions.explanation: A NIC (Network Interface Card) connects a computer to a network (LAN, WAN, or the Internet) via Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: Bluetooth is a _______ technology for short-range communication
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology (typically up to 10 meters) used to connect devices like phones, headphones, keyboards, mice.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: An SSD is faster than an HDD because _______
questions.explanation: SSD (Solid State Drive) is faster than HDD (Hard Disk Drive) because it has no moving parts — data is stored in flash memory chips, not on a spinning disk.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.prompt: The first commercial computer was _______
questions.explanation: UNIVAC I (Universal Automatic Computer I), delivered in 1951, was the first commercial computer produced in the USA. It was used by the US Census Bureau.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The highest point in Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Chappal Waddi (also called Chappal Hendu), at about 2,419m (7,936ft), is the highest point in Nigeria, located in Taraba State near the Cameroon border.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The largest lake in Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Lake Chad is the largest lake in Nigeria (shared with Chad, Niger, and Cameroon). Kainji Lake is the largest man-made lake, created by the Kainji Dam.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria is located in which continent?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is in West Africa, in the African continent. It is bordered by Benin (west), Niger (north), Chad (northeast), and Cameroon (east).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria lies between latitudes _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria lies between approximately 4°N and 14°N latitude, and between 2°E and 15°E longitude.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Yoruba people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Yoruba are mainly in South-Western Nigeria — Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Osun, Ondo, and Ekiti states.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Igbo people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Igbo are mainly in South-Eastern Nigeria — Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo states.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Hausa people are predominantly found in _______
questions.explanation: The Hausa are mainly in Northern Nigeria — states like Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Jigawa, Zamfara, Sokoto, and Kebbi.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The traditional title given to the Yoruba king is _______
questions.explanation: Yoruba kings are traditionally called Oba. Igbo kings are called Igwe or Eze. Hausa traditional rulers are called Emir.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The major source of revenue for the Nigerian government is _______
questions.explanation: Oil and gas accounts for the majority of Nigeria's government revenue and export earnings, although agriculture employs more people.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria is the largest producer of _______ in Africa
questions.explanation: Nigeria is the world's largest producer of cassava. It is also a major producer of yam, maize, and other crops.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Nigerian currency is called _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian currency is the Naira (₦), subdivided into 100 kobo. It was introduced in 1973, replacing the Nigerian pound.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital market in Nigeria is regulated by the _______
questions.explanation: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regulates the capital market. The Nigerian Stock Exchange (now Nigerian Exchange Group) is the platform where stocks are traded.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The family is the basic _______ of society
questions.explanation: The family is universally recognized as the basic unit of society. It is where children are socialized and values are transmitted.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The extended family system in Nigeria involves _______
questions.explanation: The extended family includes grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins, in addition to the nuclear family. It is a key feature of African social structure.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Marriage is a _______ between a man and a woman
questions.explanation: Marriage is a recognized social institution that establishes rights and obligations between spouses, and between the family and the wider community.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The first Prime Minister of Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was Nigeria's first Prime Minister (1960-1966). He led the country to independence.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Second Republic in Nigeria began in _______
questions.explanation: The Second Republic began in 1979 with the return to civilian rule and the election of Shehu Shagari as President. It ended with a military coup in 1983.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Third Republic was never fully implemented in Nigeria because _______
questions.explanation: General Ibrahim Babangida annulled the June 12, 1993 presidential election widely believed to have been won by M.K.O. Abiola. This ended the transition to the Third Republic.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria's civil war took place between _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War (also called the Biafran War) lasted from 1967 to 1970, after the secession of the southeastern region as the Republic of Biafra.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The leader of Biafra during the civil war was _______
questions.explanation: Lt. Col. Emeka Odumegwu Ojukwu was the leader of the short-lived Republic of Biafra. General Yakubu Gowon led the federal side.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The First Republic of Nigeria was cut short by a military coup in _______
questions.explanation: The First Republic (1963-1966) ended with the military coup of January 15, 1966, led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu and others.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: M.K.O. Abiola is famous for _______

options.text: being the first military Head of State

questions.explanation: Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale (M.K.O.) Abiola won the June 12, 1993 presidential election, which was annulled. June 12 is now celebrated as Democracy Day in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Niger River flows into the _______
questions.explanation: The Niger River flows southward through Nigeria and empties into the Atlantic Ocean through a large delta in southern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Benue River is a tributary of the _______
questions.explanation: The Benue River is the largest tributary of the Niger River. The two rivers meet at Lokoja in Kogi State.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The main vegetation zones in Nigeria include _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria has multiple vegetation zones: mangrove swamp (coast), rainforest (south), guinea savanna (middle), sudan savanna, and sahel (far north).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Zuma Rock is located in _______
questions.explanation: Zuma Rock is a large monolith located in Madalla, Niger State, Nigeria, near the capital Abuja.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The highest mountain in West Africa is located in _______
questions.explanation: Mount Cameroon (4,040m) is the highest peak in West Africa, located in the Republic of Cameroon near the Nigerian border.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Eid-el-Fitr is celebrated by _______
questions.explanation: Eid-el-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast) is celebrated by Muslims at the end of Ramadan, the holy month of fasting.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Christmas is celebrated on _______
questions.explanation: Christmas is celebrated annually on December 25 by Christians worldwide to mark the birth of Jesus Christ.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Durbar festival is a cultural event in _______
questions.explanation: Durbar is a colorful cultural festival celebrated mainly in Northern Nigerian cities like Kano, Katsina, Zaria, and Sokoto, especially during Eid celebrations.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Cocoa is mainly produced in which part of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Cocoa is mainly produced in South-Western Nigeria — Ondo, Osun, Ogun, Oyo, and Ekiti states. Nigeria is among the world's largest cocoa producers.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Petroleum was first discovered in commercial quantity in Nigeria in _______
questions.explanation: Petroleum was first discovered in commercial quantity in 1956 at Oloibiri in present-day Bayelsa State by Shell-BP. This was the start of Nigeria's oil industry.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The headquarters of ECOWAS is in _______
questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has its headquarters in Abuja, Nigeria, established in 1975.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is located in _______
questions.explanation: The CBN was established in 1958 and is headquartered in Abuja. It is the apex regulatory body of Nigeria's banking sector.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Traditional rulers play an important role in _______
questions.explanation: Traditional rulers (Obas, Emirs, Chiefs) play important roles in preserving culture, settling disputes, and promoting community development in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Yoruba word for the market is _______
questions.explanation: In Yoruba, market is 'Oja'. Eze is Igbo for king. Kasuwa is Hausa for market. These terms show the linguistic diversity of Nigeria.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The First Republic ended with the military coup of _______
questions.explanation: The First Republic (1963-1966) was overthrown by the military coup of January 15, 1966, led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu and others.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Second Republic ended with the military coup of _______
questions.explanation: The Second Republic (1979-1983) ended with the military coup of December 31, 1983, led by General Muhammadu Buhari.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Third Republic was truncated by the annulment of the _______ election
questions.explanation: The Third Republic transition was ended by General Babangida's annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election widely believed won by M.K.O. Abiola.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Fourth Republic began in _______
questions.explanation: The Fourth Republic began on May 29, 1999, with the inauguration of President Olusegun Obasanjo under the 1999 Constitution.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The 36 states of Nigeria were last created in _______
questions.explanation: The 36-state structure was created in 1996 by General Sani Abacha's regime. Earlier: 12 (1967), 19 (1976), 21 (1987), 30 (1991).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Nigerian-Biafran war was fought to keep Nigeria _______
questions.explanation: The 1967-1970 war was fought to maintain Nigeria's unity after Biafra's declaration of secession. Nigeria remained one country.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Aburi Accord was an attempt to resolve the crisis leading to the _______
questions.explanation: The Aburi Accord (Ghana, 1967) attempted to resolve the constitutional crisis between the federal government and the eastern region. Its failure contributed to the civil war.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Who was the Head of State during the Second Republic?
questions.explanation: Shehu Shagari was the President during the Second Republic (1979-1983). Obasanjo was Head of State 1976-1979, before the Second Republic.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital of Lagos State is _______
questions.explanation: Ikeja is the capital of Lagos State. Lagos Island and Victoria Island are parts of Lagos but not the state capital.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital of Kano State is _______
questions.explanation: Kano city is the capital of Kano State, in North-Western Nigeria. It is one of the oldest cities in sub-Saharan Africa.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The largest city in Nigeria by population is _______
questions.explanation: Lagos is Nigeria's largest city (and one of the largest in Africa), with over 20 million people in the metropolitan area.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The largest state in Nigeria by land area is _______
questions.explanation: Niger State is the largest by land area (~76,363 km²), followed by Borno, Taraba, and Bauchi.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The smallest state in Nigeria by land area is _______
questions.explanation: Lagos is the smallest state by area (~3,577 km²), making it the most densely populated.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The highest rainfall in Nigeria is received in the _______
questions.explanation: The South-South (coastal) region receives the highest rainfall (over 3,000mm/year in some areas). The North receives the least.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The driest region in Nigeria is the _______
questions.explanation: The Sahel (far north) is the driest region, with low rainfall and sparse vegetation.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The major religion practiced in Northern Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Islam is the dominant religion in Northern Nigeria, while Christianity is dominant in the South. Both coexist with traditional religions.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The major religion practiced in Southern Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Christianity is the dominant religion in Southern Nigeria, especially in the South-East and South-West.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Igbo traditional marriage is called _______
questions.explanation: Igba Nkwu is the traditional marriage ceremony of the Igbo people. It involves the presentation of wine and other items.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Yoruba traditional wedding ceremony is called _______
questions.explanation: Yoruba traditional marriage involves the Introduction (isijade) and the Engagement (idi-igbeyawo), with the bride's family receiving items from the groom.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Hausa traditional wedding is called _______
questions.explanation: The Hausa Muslim wedding is called Fatiha (or Nikkah) — a religious ceremony with the bride's family receiving items and the Imam officiating.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The main occupation in rural Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: Subsistence farming is the main occupation in rural Nigeria, employing over 35% of the workforce.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria's main export crop is _______
questions.explanation: Crude petroleum is Nigeria's main export, accounting for over 80% of export earnings. Cocoa and palm oil are also significant.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Stock Exchange is now called the _______
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Stock Exchange was renamed the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) in 2021 after demutualization.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is measured in _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria's GDP is reported in Naira (₦). International comparisons are often made in US dollars.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) regulates the _______
questions.explanation: The NCC regulates telecommunications in Nigeria. CBN regulates banking, NNPC regulates oil, NUC regulates universities.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The nuclear family consists of _______
questions.explanation: The nuclear family consists of parents and their children. The extended family includes grandparents, uncles, aunts, and cousins.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The head of a Nigerian family is traditionally the _______
questions.explanation: Traditionally, the man/father is considered the head of the family in most Nigerian cultures, though this is changing with modern gender equality.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: A nuclear family is also called a _______ family
questions.explanation: A nuclear family is also called a conjugal family, based on marriage between two partners and their children.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The extended family system promotes _______
questions.explanation: The extended family system in Nigeria promotes unity, cooperation, and mutual support among family members.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The National Assembly is composed of the Senate and the _______
questions.explanation: The National Assembly has two chambers: the Senate (109 members, 3 per state + FCT) and the House of Representatives (360 members).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: A Senator in Nigeria represents a _______
questions.explanation: Each Senator represents one of Nigeria's 109 senatorial districts (3 per state + 1 for FCT).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Speaker of the House of Representatives is the _______
questions.explanation: The Speaker is the presiding officer of the House of Representatives. The Senate President presides over the Senate.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The first military Head of State in Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: General J.T.U. Aguiyi-Ironsi was the first military Head of State (January-July 1966) after the first military coup in January 1966.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The second military Head of State was _______
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon became the second military Head of State in July 1966 after the counter-coup that killed Aguiyi-Ironsi. He led Nigeria during the civil war.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The third military Head of State of Nigeria was _______
questions.explanation: General Murtala Mohammed became Head of State in July 1975 after a coup that overthrew Gowon. He was assassinated in February 1976.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Who succeeded Murtala Mohammed as Head of State?
questions.explanation: General Olusegun Obasanjo succeeded Murtala Mohammed in February 1976 after Murtala was assassinated. He handed over power to civilian rule in 1979.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The first military coup in Nigeria occurred on _______
questions.explanation: The first military coup took place on January 15, 1966, led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu and others, overthrowing the First Republic.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The British colonial rule in Nigeria officially began with the _______ of 1861
questions.explanation: Britain formally annexed Lagos in 1861, marking the beginning of colonial rule in Nigeria. Earlier: trading activities from 1800s.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The protectorate of Northern Nigeria was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Northern Nigeria Protectorate was established on January 1, 1900, with Frederick Lugard as High Commissioner.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The protectorate of Southern Nigeria was established in _______
questions.explanation: The Southern Nigeria Protectorate was established in 1900, originally called the 'Niger Coast Protectorate' (renamed in 1906).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria took place on _______
questions.explanation: The amalgamation of Northern and Southern Protectorates was on January 1, 1914, by Lord Lugard, creating the colony and protectorate of Nigeria.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The first Executive Governor of Lagos State was _______
questions.explanation: Chief Lateef Jakande was the first civilian Governor of Lagos State (1979-1983) during the Second Republic.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The first military Governor of Lagos State was _______
questions.explanation: Colonel Adekunle Fajuyi was the first military Governor of the Western Region after the 1966 coup.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria's National Archives is located in _______
questions.explanation: The National Archives of Nigeria is in Ibadan, Oyo State. It preserves important historical documents and records.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The National Museum in Lagos is famous for its collection of _______
questions.explanation: The National Museum Lagos houses Nigerian art, traditional artifacts, archaeological finds, and the famous Igbo-Ukwu bronze artifacts.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Yoruba people are known for their traditional _______
questions.explanation: The Yoruba are known for the talking drum (gangan), the Bata drum, and other musical instruments, as well as Ifa divination and Yoruba art.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Igbo people are famous for their _______
questions.explanation: The Igbo are famous for their bronze and brass artwork (like the Igbo-Ukwu bronzes from the 9th century) and their trade and commerce.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Hausa-Fulani are known for their _______
questions.explanation: The Hausa-Fulani are known for their leatherwork, embroidery (especially babban riga and abaya), weaving, and agricultural practices.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital of Oyo State is _______
questions.explanation: Ibadan is the capital of Oyo State. It's one of the largest cities in West Africa, located in south-western Nigeria.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital of Rivers State is _______
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt is the capital of Rivers State, in the South-South geopolitical zone. It's a major oil and gas hub.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital of Borno State is _______
questions.explanation: Maiduguri is the capital of Borno State in North-East Nigeria. It's a major trading center on the Lake Chad region.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital of Delta State is _______
questions.explanation: Asaba is the capital of Delta State. The state is a major oil-producing area in the Niger Delta.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The population of Nigeria (as of 2023 estimates) is approximately _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa, with over 200 million people (2023 estimates). It is among the top 10 most populous countries in the world.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The official language of Nigeria is _______
questions.explanation: English is the official language of Nigeria, inherited from British colonial rule. It is used for government, business, and formal education.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria's main ethnic groups are _______
questions.explanation: The three major ethnic groups are Hausa (in the north), Yoruba (in the south-west), and Igbo (in the south-east). Together they make up over 50% of Nigeria's population.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Nigerian economy is the _______ largest in Africa
questions.explanation: Nigeria has one of the largest economies in Africa (rebased in 2014, it became the largest economy in Africa by GDP).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: Nigeria is a member of _______
questions.explanation: Nigeria is a member of many international organizations: OPEC (Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries), ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States), AU (African Union), UN (United Nations), and others.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The capital of South Africa is _______
questions.explanation: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), Bloemfontein (judicial).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The African Union (AU) headquarters is in _______
questions.explanation: The African Union (AU) has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The AU was established in 2002, replacing the Organization of African Unity (OAU).

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The United Nations headquarters is in _______
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York City, USA. The UN was founded in 1945 after World War II.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: The Commonwealth of Nations includes _______
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of 56 countries, mostly former territories of the British Empire. Nigeria is a member.

questions.subject: Social Studies
questions.prompt: A natural resource is a _______ found in nature that is useful to humans
questions.explanation: A natural resource is any material or substance (e.g., oil, gold, water, timber) found in nature that humans use for economic or other purposes.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural form: child
questions.explanation: Children is the correct plural of child.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: Sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which word is a noun?
questions.explanation: Garden is a person, place, or thing — a noun.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct spelling:
questions.explanation: The word receive follows the i-before-e rule (except after c).

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What is the opposite of ancient?
questions.explanation: Ancient means very old; modern means recent or new.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: There are ___ books on the table.
questions.explanation: Some is used with plural countable nouns in positive statements.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with cat?
questions.explanation: Hat rhymes with cat — both end with the -at sound.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct article?
questions.explanation: An is used before words beginning with a vowel sound. Honest starts with a vowel sound.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which word is a verb?
questions.explanation: Jump describes an action — it is a verb.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The dog ___ under the tree.
questions.explanation: With the dog (singular subject), the verb takes s.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What is the past tense of go?
questions.explanation: Went is the irregular past tense of go.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which word is a pronoun?
questions.explanation: She replaces a noun — it is a pronoun.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Identify the adjective in: The tall boy ran fast.
questions.explanation: Tall describes the boy — it is an adjective.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which of these is a compound word?
questions.explanation: Sunshine is made of two words: sun + shine.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct preposition: The cat is ___ the table.
questions.explanation: On indicates the cat is resting on top of the table surface.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: The teacher gave the students __ assignment. Choose the correct article.
questions.explanation: An is used before words beginning with a vowel sound. Assignment starts with the sound a.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Identify the verb in: She quietly opened the door.
questions.explanation: Opened is the action word (verb) in this sentence.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a metaphor?
questions.explanation: The sea was a mirror compares the sea to a mirror without using like or as — a metaphor.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What type of noun is Abuja?
questions.explanation: Abuja is the name of a specific city — a proper noun.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct tense: By next year, she ___ in Lagos for five years.
questions.explanation: Will have lived is the future perfect — action completed by a specific future time.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb?
questions.explanation: Slowly describes how an action is done — it is an adverb.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Identify the subject in: The young girls sang at the festival.
questions.explanation: The young girls is the subject — the ones performing the action.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses direct speech correctly?

options.text: She said that she was tired.

questions.explanation: Direct speech uses quotation marks and the exact words of the speaker.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct conditional: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay indoors.
questions.explanation: In first conditional sentences, we use the present simple after if for future possibilities.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What figure of speech is The wind howled?
questions.explanation: Wind cannot howl — this gives human qualities to the wind, making it personification.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which of these is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: Team refers to a group of people — a collective noun.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive voice: Someone has stolen my bag.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the object becomes the subject.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: Him and I went to school.
He and I went to school.
Him and me went to school.
He and me went to school.

questions.explanation: He and I are the correct subject pronouns to use as the subject of a sentence.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Identify the antonym of generous:
questions.explanation: Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which prefix means not or opposite?
questions.explanation: Un- is a negative prefix meaning not (e.g., unhappy, unhealthy).

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What is the comparative form of good?
questions.explanation: Good is an irregular adjective — its comparative form is better.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence contains a homophone error?

options.text: I can see the sea from here.

questions.explanation: Past is a noun/time word; the verb form should be passed.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What does acronym mean?

options.text: a word formed from the first letters of a phrase
a shortened form of a word

questions.explanation: An acronym is formed from the initial letters of a phrase, e.g., JAMB.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of an interjection?
questions.explanation: Oh! expresses emotion and stands alone — it is an interjection.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct conjunction: She studied hard ___ she passed.
questions.explanation: Because shows a reason — she studied hard as a result of wanting to pass.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What is the superlative form of bad?
questions.explanation: Bad is irregular — its superlative form is worst.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Identify the transitive verb:
questions.explanation: Eat takes a direct object (e.g., eat food) — it is transitive.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses fewer correctly?
questions.explanation: Fewer is used for countable nouns; less is for uncountable nouns.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: What is a palindrome?

options.text: a word that reads the same backwards and forwards

questions.explanation: A palindrome reads the same backwards and forwards, e.g., level, radar.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun: The girl ___ won the prize is my sister.
questions.explanation: Who is used for people as the subject of a relative clause.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to benevolent:
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kind.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a compound sentence?

options.text: Because it rained, we stayed inside.

questions.explanation: A compound sentence has two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which option contains a dangling modifier?

options.text: Walking down the street, the shop looked attractive.
After reading the book, the movie was disappointing.
Being late, the meeting was difficult to follow.

questions.explanation: All sentences above have modifiers that do not clearly attach to the subject of the main clause.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Identify the semantic relationship: parent : child
questions.explanation: A parent and child are hyponyms — specific types of a broader category.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the subjunctive mood correctly?

options.text: If I was you, I would go.
